# `custom`
# (provider-config JSON validated in the resolve step; key only from
# FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY). The setup job's resolve step is a byte-consistent
# copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 step — keep both in sync (cross-reference
# comment in both files). With the z.ai budget at zero, the kimi path is
# what keeps this workflow dispatchable.
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY      — kimi coding key for kimi-for-coding (the model
#                            id is the plan name; shared with bench.yml;
#                            never the review factory's KIMI_REVIEW_KEY)
#   FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY    — key for provider=custom, injected as FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

run-name: fa bench-harbor · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1503, same contract as bench.yml gh-1471: default = pre-gh-1503 behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1503 (bench.yml gh-1471 D1/AC 2a): ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Terminal-Bench family: label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or full Harbor id (see bench/harbor_fa/families.py); default 2.1 (issue #1316)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      attempts:
        description: 'harbor --n-attempts per trial (-k)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      n-concurrent:
        description: 'harbor --n-concurrent trials (1 = z.ai rate-limit safe; the kimi coding plan tolerates more — owner picks at dispatch)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count for CPU tasks (~4 tasks/shard keeps each job under the 6h window)'
        required: false
        default: '16'
      cpu-env:
        description: 'Harbor env for CPU shards (docker default — issue #1316; modal for the self-hosted path)'
        required: false
        default: 'docker'
      cpu-runner:
        description: 'Runner label hosting the harbor CLI (ubuntu-latest default — GH runners ship docker; self-hosted for the modal path)'
        required: false
        default: 'ubuntu-latest'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared task caps)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds the runner for hours; queue a second dispatch
# instead of stacking them. One group across the whole family: harbor
# runs serialize even when different dataset versions are dispatched
# back-to-back.
concurrency:
  group: bench-harbor
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & shard dataset
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      cpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.cpu_count }}
      gpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.gpu_count }}
      family: ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }}
      dataset: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # gh-1503: byte-consistent copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 resolve step
      # (same run block, same outputs) — the single-source extraction was
      # rejected there to keep the workflow self-contained; the
      # cross-reference comment in both files is the sync contract. Maps
      # the provider choice to the full provider triple (type/baseUrl/
      # model/key env) and preflights the selected secret BEFORE the
      # bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
      # must cost one setup minute, not shard-hours of 429s. Presence
      # only: the value is never echoed (the ::add-mask line masks its
      # base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into the container).
      # An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a silent fallthrough
      # to the zai default. REG-1: the default resolves the exact
      # 3-field zai config bench-harbor.yml hardcoded before gh-1503.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          # bench.yml reads this from its top-level env block; harbor has
          # no other consumer, so the value lives here (single spelling,
          # same as bench.yml's BENCH_MODEL).
          BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              # The model id IS the plan name (owner correction, gh-1471
              # follow-up): the coding endpoint serves it as
              # 'kimi-for-coding', not k3-256k.
              model='kimi-for-coding'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # model == choice by construction — no doubled label.
              run_label="kimi-for-coding"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `apiKeyEnvVar` is injected by this step (fixed
              # FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM), never accepted from the input — a
              # user-supplied value would be silently overridden (checked
              # before the key-like scan below, which would otherwise
              # flag the field first with a less precise message).
              if printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'has("apiKeyEnvVar")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not declare apiKeyEnvVar — the resolve step injects it as the fixed FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM; the key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught. The scan
              # descends into nested objects: a key field name pasted
              # inside a header map rides through a top-level-only scan
              # exactly like a top-level one.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [.. | objects | keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | unique | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Closed key whitelist, mirroring the Dart _parseConfig
              # consumer (baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow,
              # maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel): an unknown or typo'd
              # key would otherwise fail loud at every trial's container
              # boot after shards start. `type` is allowed here (it rides
              # the FA_PROVIDER_TYPE output) but stripped from the
              # emitted config below.
              unsupported=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                [. | keys[]
                  | select(. as $k
                      | ["baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens","input","thinkingLevel","type"]
                      | index($k) | not)]
                  | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$unsupported" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config has unsupported key(s): $unsupported — supported keys: baseUrl, model, contextWindow, maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel (type selects FA_PROVIDER_TYPE and is not echoed into FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `type` feeds the container's catalog lookup via
              # FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: when declared it must be a non-empty
              # string (jq's `//` treats "" as present, so an explicit
              # check is required); undeclared/null defaults to the
              # openai-compatible catalog entry.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("type") and .type != null then (.type | type == "string" and test("\\S")) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"type\" must be a non-empty string naming a catalog provider (e.g. \"openai\") when declared"; exit 1
              fi
              # The capability pair mirrors _parseCapabilityInt: JSON
              # integers at or above the Dart resolver floors
              # (minOverrideContextWindow 16384 / minOverrideMaxTokens
              # 1024 — the same boundaries as the yaml overrides layer);
              # blank string / null are ABSENT, like every other optional
              # input; anything else throws at container boot today.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '
                def capok(min): . as $v
                  | $v == null or (($v | type) == "string" and ($v | test("^\\s*$")))
                  or (($v | type) == "number" and ($v | floor) == $v and $v >= min);
                (.contextWindow | capok(16384)) and (.maxTokens | capok(1024))
              ' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config contextWindow/maxTokens must be integers at or above the Dart resolver floors (contextWindow >= 16384, maxTokens >= 1024) — a below-floor or non-integer declaration would fail loud at every trial's container boot"; exit 1
              fi
              # `input` mirrors _parseInputList: a non-empty list whose
              # entries are exactly "text"/"image".
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("input") then (.input | type == "array" and length > 0 and all(.[]; . == "text" or . == "image")) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"input\" must be a non-empty list of \"text\"/\"image\" entries (the Dart preconfig's contract)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `thinkingLevel` mirrors _parseThinkingLevel: a blank
              # string is absent; otherwise one of the
              # configThinkingLevels ladder (xhigh/max fold to high
              # Dart-side).
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("thinkingLevel") then (.thinkingLevel | if type == "string" then (test("^\\s*$") or (. as $l | ["minimal","low","medium","high","xhigh","max"] | index($l) != null)) else false end) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"thinkingLevel\" must be one of minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max (the Dart preconfig's ladder)"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the
              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1
                fi
              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1
              fi
              # Passthrough: every declared field rides the config
              # verbatim EXCEPT "type" — it already rides the dedicated
              # FA_PROVIDER_TYPE output/env, and the Dart preconfig's
              # FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG whitelist has no "type" key (it would
              # throw at every trial's container boot). Blank/null
              # capability fields are dropped (Dart-side they are
              # ABSENT, like every other optional input — the emitted
              # config declares only what is effective). Plus the fixed
              # key-env injection; `type` defaults to the
              # openai-compatible catalog entry.
              provider_type=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.type // "openai"')
              model=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.model')
              provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" '
                del(.type)
                | del(.contextWindow | select(. == null or ((. | type) == "string" and (. | test("^\\s*$")))))
                | del(.maxTokens | select(. == null or ((. | type) == "string" and (. | test("^\\s*$")))))
                | . + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')
              run_label="custom ($model)"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash', 'kimi-for-coding' or 'custom'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ -z "$secret_value" ]; then
            echo "::error::provider $PROVIDER selected but secret $secret_name is not set"; exit 1
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded;
          # GitHub auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$secret_value" | base64 -w0)"
          {
            echo "provider_type=$provider_type"
            echo "provider_config=$provider_config"
            echo "provider_key_env=$key_env"
            echo "bench_model=$model"
            echo "run_label=$run_label"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # stable satisfies the repo SDK constraint (>=3.12.0 <4.0.0).
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

      # Resolve the dispatch input (family label, bare version, or full
      # Harbor id) to the canonical dataset id; unknown or version-less
      # specs fail fast here, before any download.
      - name: Resolve Terminal-Bench family
        id: family
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ inputs.dataset }}
        run: python bench/harbor_fa/families.py resolve "$DATASET"

      # Cost guard (issue #1124 E3): full runs of the intermediate
      # families are hours of GPU + LLM spend — require explicit
      # confirmation. Smoke runs (non-empty tasks) and 4.0 (the
      # historical default, AC4) are unaffected.
      - name: Confirm full intermediate-family run
        if: steps.family.outputs.family != '4.0' && inputs.confirm-full-run != true
        env:
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
        run: |
          # split_tasks.py strips each comma-glob before use, so " ", ",",
          # " , " all normalize to zero globs = a FULL dataset run. Judge
          # emptiness on that same normalization, not the raw input.
          if [ -z "$(printf %s "$TASKS" | tr -d '[:space:],')" ]; then
            echo "::error::Full run of Terminal-Bench ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }} (${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}, ~${{ steps.family.outputs.tasks }} tasks x $ATTEMPTS attempts) requires confirm-full-run: true. Smoke first: tasks=${{ steps.family.outputs.smoke }}, attempts=1 (docs/bench.md)."
            exit 1
          fi

      # Same bundle as bench/terminal_bench/run.sh: tar the bundle/ dir so
      # the adapter extracts bin/fah at the top level of /opt/fa.
      - name: Build fa CLI bundle (Linux)
        run: |
          bundle_dir="$(mktemp -d)/fa-bundle"
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output="$bundle_dir"
          tar -czf fa-bundle.tar.gz -C "$bundle_dir/bundle" .

      - name: Upload fa bundle
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle
          path: fa-bundle.tar.gz

      # terminal-bench-era note: harbor is fine on 3.13; typer-based CLIs
      # break on 3.14.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned: the adapter targets the 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent contract.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'

      # Same gate as bench.yml: stdlib-only bench script tests. Two
      # discovery roots: bench/terminal_bench (legacy scripts + the
      # harbor parity suite from #1122 — terminal-bench is installed
      # just for the legacy-adapter import surface) and bench/harbor_fa
      # (the #1124 family/summary suites + the #1123 token/cost summary
      # tests). Discovering bench/ itself would need __init__.py
      # plumbing the bench dirs don't have.
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
        run: |
          pip install 'terminal-bench==0.2.18'
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v

      # Download the dataset once for classification; harbor re-fetches
      # into its own cache during the run. DATASET is the canonical id
      # resolved by the family step (the raw input may be a bare label).
      - name: Shard dataset into CPU / GPU shards
        id: shards
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          SHARDS: ${{ inputs.shards }}
          CPU_ENV: ${{ inputs.cpu-env }}
        run: |
          harbor datasets download "$DATASET" --output-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/ds" --overwrite
          # Dataset name at version: dir name is the dataset slug.
          ds_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/ds/$(basename "${DATASET%%@*}")"
          [ -d "$ds_dir" ] || ds_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/ds"
          # split_tasks.py writes the matrix/counts into GITHUB_OUTPUT itself.
          # harbor -i matches qualified ids (<org>/<name>): prefix with the
          # org part of the dataset spec.
          python bench/harbor_fa/split_tasks.py "$ds_dir" \
            --filter "$TASKS" --shards "$SHARDS" --cpu-env "$CPU_ENV" \
            --task-prefix "${DATASET%%/*}/"

  bench:
    name: fa on tbench ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}, shard ${{ matrix.i }} (${{ matrix.env }}, ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }})
    needs: setup
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.cpu-runner }}
    # ~4 tasks/shard x --n-attempts x task runtime (tbench agent caps
    # reach 8h but typical runs are far shorter) with headroom; the
    # self-hosted runner has no 6h hosted-runner cap to trip over.
    timeout-minutes: 355
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      max-parallel: 5
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.setup.outputs.matrix) }}
    env:
      FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
      DATASET: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.dataset }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download fa bundle
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle

      # The optional self-hosted runner is a macOS box: setup-python cannot
      # write the hosted tool cache there (mkdir /Users/runner denied) and the
      # runner's own python3 is 3.14 — typer-based CLIs (harbor) break on 3.14.
      # The uv-managed CPython 3.13 user-space install below works on BOTH
      # runner kinds (the ubuntu-latest default included); uv is also the
      # canonical harbor install per the 4.0 docs.
      - name: Install harbor (uv-managed python 3.13)
        run: |
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          command -v uv >/dev/null || curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          uv venv --python 3.13 .bench-venv
          uv pip install --python .bench-venv/bin/python 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'
          .bench-venv/bin/python -c 'import sys; print("venv python:", sys.version.split()[0])'

      - name: Run harbor (fa agent, ${{ matrix.env }} env)
        env:
          FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-bundle.tar.gz
          PYTHONPATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/bench/harbor_fa
          # gh-1503: the provider triple is resolved once in the setup
          # job (preflighted secret + hard fail on an unmapped choice) —
          # the shard only consumes it. All three bench keys are mapped
          # here (custom's AC 2a: key only from FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY); the
          # run block picks the resolved one by name, fa_agent.py ships
          # exactly that key into the container.
          FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_type }}
          FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_config }}
          FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_key_env }}
          FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
          MODAL_TOKEN_ID: ${{ secrets.MODAL_TOKEN_ID }}
          MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET: ${{ secrets.MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET }}
          HARBOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HARBOR_API_KEY }}
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
          NCONC: ${{ inputs.n-concurrent }}
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          # No step-level DATASET here: a step env overrides the job env,
          # and a steps.* ref to the setup job's family step evaluates

"""Terminal-Bench adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Follows the AbstractInstalledAgent pattern (same as the claude-code agent):
a setup script installs fa inside the task container, and the agent runs as
`fa -p "<instruction>"` in the container's tmux session, so fa's bash/read/
write tools operate on the container filesystem.

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah + lib/),
                         extracted to /opt/fa by the setup script.
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64) — the object may
                         also declare the optional capability pair
                         "contextWindow"/"maxTokens" (gh-1471 D4: bench's
                         kimi mapping pins 200000/16384 so a catalog drift
                         can never silently truncate the served window;
                         absent fields keep the catalog defaults).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122, see bench/fa_agent_timeout.py): when any
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER is set, perform_task takes over the outer
  agent deadline from the harness's flat wait_for: the agent runs under a
  progress-aware ladder (silent => die at the base cap as today; output
  flowing => deadline recedes up to the hard ceiling). With no knobs set
  this module delegates to the stock AbstractInstalledAgent.perform_task
  byte-for-byte (historical comparability, issue #1122 REG-1).

  Round 3 (issue #1392): when FA_STALL_GAP_SEC or
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC activates the progress-watch mode, the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch (progressing trials die
  only at the absolute ceiling; a >= stall-gap gap is a provable stall).
  Every trial also gets: live per-request lines as they happen
  (LiveProgress over the pane's FA_CONN events), a per-trial
  bench_metrics.json (latency p50/p95, watchdog fires, fresh-vs-reused),
  a hang-*.json forensics dump on a stall verdict BEFORE the kill lands
  (StallSentinel), and an export-guard.json row when the agent produced
  output but the session export came back empty (ExportGuard).

  gh-1430 — the ordering invariant this adapter operates under:

      fa's watchdog is the sole arbiter of stream death; the bench gap
      only catches pane/process death.

  fa errors a truly dead provider stream itself at
  providerStreamIdleTimeout (300s, lib/src/providers/provider_common.dart)
  and, since gh-1430, heartbeats `… reasoning Ns (streaming)` to the pane
  while its stream emits events the headless output mode does not render.
  The shipped stall gap (360s = watchdog + margin, bench/fa_agent_timeout.py)
  therefore fires only when the PANE went silent — process death or a
  wedged pane — never while fa itself considers the stream live. The REG
  in test_fa_agent_timeout.py pins the gap >= watchdog against the Dart
  source and fails if either side drifts.

  Issue #1406 (never-again): the launch line itself carries the
  non-secret FA_CONN_* env into the tmux pane (`export …; env |
  grep FA_CONN > /tmp/fa-conn-env.txt;` prefix — pane env belongs to the
  shell/server history, not to the step env that typed a later command),
  the capture folds into agent-logs/fa-conn-env.txt as runtime proof,
  and the loud-empty guard fires (conn-guard.json + a ::warning::
  annotation) when a trial's bench_metrics.json has requests == []
  despite real usage tokens — an instrumentation outage is never silent.

  PYTHONPATH=bench/terminal_bench tb run -d terminal-bench-core==0.1.1 \

on:

"""Terminal-Bench adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Follows the AbstractInstalledAgent pattern (same as the claude-code agent):
a setup script installs fa inside the task container, and the agent runs as
`fa -p "<instruction>"` in the container's tmux session, so fa's bash/read/
write tools operate on the container filesystem.

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah + lib/),
                         extracted to /opt/fa by the setup script.
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64) — the object may
                         also declare the optional capability pair
                         "contextWindow"/"maxTokens" (gh-1471 D4: bench's
                         kimi mapping pins 200000/16384 so a catalog drift
                         can never silently truncate the served window;
                         absent fields keep the catalog defaults).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122, see bench/fa_agent_timeout.py): when any
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER is set, perform_task takes over the outer
  agent deadline from the harness's flat wait_for: the agent runs under a
  progress-aware ladder (silent => die at the base cap as today; output
  flowing => deadline recedes up to the hard ceiling). With no knobs set
  this module delegates to the stock AbstractInstalledAgent.perform_task
  byte-for-byte (historical comparability, issue #1122 REG-1).

  Round 3 (issue #1392): when FA_STALL_GAP_SEC or
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC activates the progress-watch mode, the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch (progressing trials die
  only at the absolute ceiling; a >= stall-gap gap is a provable stall).
  Every trial also gets: live per-request lines as they happen
  (LiveProgress over the pane's FA_CONN events), a per-trial
  bench_metrics.json (latency p50/p95, watchdog fires, fresh-vs-reused),
  a hang-*.json forensics dump on a stall verdict BEFORE the kill lands
  (StallSentinel), and an export-guard.json row when the agent produced
  output but the session export came back empty (ExportGuard).

  gh-1430 — the ordering invariant this adapter operates under:

      fa's watchdog is the sole arbiter of stream death; the bench gap
      only catches pane/process death.

  fa errors a truly dead provider stream itself at
  providerStreamIdleTimeout (300s, lib/src/providers/provider_common.dart)
  and, since gh-1430, heartbeats `… reasoning Ns (streaming)` to the pane
  while its stream emits events the headless output mode does not render.
  The shipped stall gap (360s = watchdog + margin, bench/fa_agent_timeout.py)
  therefore fires only when the PANE went silent — process death or a
  wedged pane — never while fa itself considers the stream live. The REG
  in test_fa_agent_timeout.py pins the gap >= watchdog against the Dart
  source and fails if either side drifts.

  Issue #1406 (never-again): the launch line itself carries the
  non-secret FA_CONN_* env into the tmux pane (`export …; env |
  grep FA_CONN > /tmp/fa-conn-env.txt;` prefix — pane env belongs to the
  shell/server history, not to the step env that typed a later command),
  the capture folds into agent-logs/fa-conn-env.txt as runtime proof,
  and the loud-empty guard fires (conn-guard.json + a ::warning::
  annotation) when a trial's bench_metrics.json has requests == []
  despite real usage tokens — an instrumentation outage is never silent.

  PYTHONPATH=bench/terminal_bench tb run -d terminal-bench-core==0.1.1 \
    --agent-import-path fa_agent:FaAgent -t hello-world

Critical discovery: most `exec_run` consumers use **attribute access** (`result.exit_code`, `result.output`), while only `_fold_session_usage` (line 793) uses **tuple unpacking** (`exit_code, output = ...`).

Real docker `exec_run` returns an `ExecResult` namedtuple — `(exit_code, output)` — which supports BOTH tuple unpacking AND attribute access. So both shapes work against real docker.

The fake returns SimpleNamespace → attribute access works (the supervised tests pass), but tuple unpacking fails (the fold warning).

So the faithful fake shape is a **namedtuple** `(exit_code, output)` — like docker's ExecResult: attribute access AND unpacking both work. That's the cleanest fix: use `collections.namedtuple`-style return in `_exec_run`.

For `get_archive`: real docker returns `(bits, stat)` tuple. Production: `bits, _ = session.container.get_archive(...)`. Fake must return that tuple shape.

name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.

    inputs:

        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false

  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also

  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).

# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1638

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `test_other_failure_modes_stay_raw_in_the_stock_audit` fails on main with `FileNotFoundError: …/fa-agent-timeout.json` (bench-harbor setup job red since the Oct-14 wave), plus dozens of `session usage extraction failed` / `fa session export failed` warnings polluting the same log, plus a stale REG red in `bench/mls_bench`.

**Root cause** (three independent rots, all in `bench/`):

1. **Audit writer gap (AC1)** — `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py`, `FaAgent.perform_task`, stock/unsupervised path. The gh-1209 never-started guard
   ```python
   if result.failure_mode in _NEVER_STARTED_MODES:
       return result
   ```
   early-returns BEFORE the gh-1576 (I2) audit write. `_NEVER_STARTED_MODES = {AGENT_INSTALLATION_FAILED, UNKNOWN_AGENT_ERROR}`, so with a known external cap the audit file is never written for exactly the "other failure modes" the gh-1576 contract says must land **raw** — the `else str(result.failure_mode.value)` branch of the same audit call is dead code for those modes. The writer's own comment ("with an external cap known, even this unsupervised termination lands the audit") states the contract the early return violates. Reproduced locally with CI parity: `python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench` → `Ran 410 tests … FAILED (errors=1)`, same FileNotFoundError.

2. **Unfaithful docker fakes (AC2)** — `FakeTmuxSession.container` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`) and `FakeContainer` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_progress_watch_adapter.py`) return `types.SimpleNamespace(exit_code=…, output=…)` from `exec_run`, but docker-py's `ExecResult` is a **namedtuple** `(exit_code, output)`: production unpacks it in `_fold_session_usage` (`exit_code, output = …exec_run(…)` → "cannot unpack non-iterable types.SimpleNamespace") while reading attributes elsewhere. Both fakes also lack `get_archive` (the issue #1339 session export calls `session.container.get_archive` → "'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'get_archive'"). Not a production regression: the production call shapes match the real docker API; the fakes predate the #1339 export and the fold's unpack. ~18 warning pairs across otherwise-passing tests.

3. **Stale REG in the third bench root (AC4 blocker)** — `bench/mls_bench/test_build_run.py::RegressionPinsTest::test_bench_harbor_family_anchors` pins the pre-#1316 default dataset literal `terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0`; #1316 deliberately moved the bench-harbor default to `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest`. Same rot class as the ticket's systemic lesson: mls_bench is only executed by bench-mls.yml's dispatch-gated setup, so the drift sat invisible.

**Impact**: every bench-harbor/bench dispatch dies at setup (`errors=1`) — shards never start; the warnings bury real signal in trial logs; any PR touching bench/ ships untested python.

**Fix approach**:
1. Skip only the usage fold for never-started modes; keep the gh-1576 audit write (the raw failure-mode string IS the truthful outcome). Parity with the harbor adapter holds (harbor always writes the audit on every termination path).
2. Make both fakes faithful to docker-py: namedtuple `ExecResult` (unpack + attribute access both work) and a `get_archive` returning `([valid_tar], stat)`.
3. Update the stale REG to pin the shipped #1316 default (2.1), keeping the agent/MLS-free anchors.
4. Systemic guard: new path-filtered workflow `.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml` running the exact setup gate (same pinned deps: `harbor[modal]==0.23.0`, `terminal-bench==0.2.18`, python 3.13) on every PR and main push touching `bench/**`.

**Previous attempt**: none (first fix for gh-1638).

"""Terminal-Bench adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Follows the AbstractInstalledAgent pattern (same as the claude-code agent):
a setup script installs fa inside the task container, and the agent runs as
`fa -p "<instruction>"` in the container's tmux session, so fa's bash/read/
write tools operate on the container filesystem.

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah + lib/),
                         extracted to /opt/fa by the setup script.
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64) — the object may
                         also declare the optional capability pair
                         "contextWindow"/"maxTokens" (gh-1471 D4: bench's
                         kimi mapping pins 200000/16384 so a catalog drift
                         can never silently truncate the served window;
                         absent fields keep the catalog defaults).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122, see bench/fa_agent_timeout.py): when any
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER is set, perform_task takes over the outer
  agent deadline from the harness's flat wait_for: the agent runs under a
  progress-aware ladder (silent => die at the base cap as today; output
  flowing => deadline recedes up to the hard ceiling). With no knobs set
  this module delegates to the stock AbstractInstalledAgent.perform_task
  byte-for-byte (historical comparability, issue #1122 REG-1).

  Round 3 (issue #1392): when FA_STALL_GAP_SEC or
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC activates the progress-watch mode, the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch (progressing trials die
  only at the absolute ceiling; a >= stall-gap gap is a provable stall).
  Every trial also gets: live per-request lines as they happen
  (LiveProgress over the pane's FA_CONN events), a per-trial
  bench_metrics.json (latency p50/p95, watchdog fires, fresh-vs-reused),
  a hang-*.json forensics dump on a stall verdict BEFORE the kill lands
  (StallSentinel), and an export-guard.json row when the agent produced
  output but the session export came back empty (ExportGuard).

  gh-1430 — the ordering invariant this adapter operates under:

      fa's watchdog is the sole arbiter of stream death; the bench gap
      only catches pane/process death.

  fa errors a truly dead provider stream itself at
  providerStreamIdleTimeout (300s, lib/src/providers/provider_common.dart)
  and, since gh-1430, heartbeats `… reasoning Ns (streaming)` to the pane
  while its stream emits events the headless output mode does not render.
  The shipped stall gap (360s = watchdog + margin, bench/fa_agent_timeout.py)
  therefore fires only when the PANE went silent — process death or a
  wedged pane — never while fa itself considers the stream live. The REG
  in test_fa_agent_timeout.py pins the gap >= watchdog against the Dart
  source and fails if either side drifts.

  Issue #1406 (never-again): the launch line itself carries the
  non-secret FA_CONN_* env into the tmux pane (`export …; env |
  grep FA_CONN > /tmp/fa-conn-env.txt;` prefix — pane env belongs to the
  shell/server history, not to the step env that typed a later command),
  the capture folds into agent-logs/fa-conn-env.txt as runtime proof,
  and the loud-empty guard fires (conn-guard.json + a ::warning::
  annotation) when a trial's bench_metrics.json has requests == []
  despite real usage tokens — an instrumentation outage is never silent.

  PYTHONPATH=bench/terminal_bench tb run -d terminal-bench-core==0.1.1 \
    --agent-import-path fa_agent:FaAgent -t hello-world
"""

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1638

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `test_other_failure_modes_stay_raw_in_the_stock_audit` fails on main with `FileNotFoundError: …/fa-agent-timeout.json` (bench-harbor setup job red since the Oct-14 wave), plus dozens of `session usage extraction failed` / `fa session export failed` warnings polluting the same log, plus a stale REG red in `bench/mls_bench`.

**Root cause** (three independent rots, all in `bench/`):

1. **Audit writer gap (AC1)** — `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py`, `FaAgent.perform_task`, stock/unsupervised path. The gh-1209 never-started guard
   ```python
   if result.failure_mode in _NEVER_STARTED_MODES:
       return result
   ```
   early-returns BEFORE the gh-1576 (I2) audit write. `_NEVER_STARTED_MODES = {AGENT_INSTALLATION_FAILED, UNKNOWN_AGENT_ERROR}`, so with a known external cap the audit file is never written for exactly the "other failure modes" the gh-1576 contract says must land **raw** — the `else str(result.failure_mode.value)` branch of the same audit call is dead code for those modes. The writer's own comment ("with an external cap known, even this unsupervised termination lands the audit") states the contract the early return violates. Reproduced locally with CI parity: `python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench` → `Ran 410 tests … FAILED (errors=1)`, same FileNotFoundError.

2. **Unfaithful docker fakes (AC2)** — `FakeTmuxSession.container` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`) and `FakeContainer` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_progress_watch_adapter.py`) return `types.SimpleNamespace(exit_code=…, output=…)` from `exec_run`, but docker-py's `ExecResult` is a **namedtuple** `(exit_code, output)`: production unpacks it in `_fold_session_usage` (`exit_code, output = …exec_run(…)` → "cannot unpack non-iterable types.SimpleNamespace") while reading attributes elsewhere. Both fakes also lack `get_archive` (the issue #1339 session export calls `session.container.get_archive` → "'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'get_archive'"). Not a production regression: the production call shapes match the real docker API; the fakes predate the #1339 export and the fold's unpack. ~18 warning pairs across otherwise-passing tests.

3. **Stale REG in the third bench root (AC4 blocker)** — `bench/mls_bench/test_build_run.py::RegressionPinsTest::test_bench_harbor_family_anchors` pins the pre-#1316 default dataset literal `terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0`; #1316 deliberately moved the bench-harbor default to `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest`. Same rot class as the ticket's systemic lesson: mls_bench is only executed by bench-mls.yml's dispatch-gated setup, so the drift sat invisible.

**Impact**: every bench-harbor/bench dispatch dies at setup (`errors=1`) — shards never start; the warnings bury real signal in trial logs; any PR touching bench/ ships untested python.

**Fix approach**:
1. Skip only the usage fold for never-started modes; keep the gh-1576 audit write (the raw failure-mode string IS the truthful outcome). Parity with the harbor adapter holds (harbor always writes the audit on every termination path).
2. Make both fakes faithful to docker-py: namedtuple `ExecResult` (unpack + attribute access both work) and a `get_archive` returning `([valid_tar], stat)`.
3. Update the stale REG to pin the shipped #1316 default (2.1), keeping the agent/MLS-free anchors.
4. Systemic guard: new path-filtered workflow `.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml` running the exact setup gate (same pinned deps: `harbor[modal]==0.23.0`, `terminal-bench==0.2.18`, python 3.13) on every PR and main push touching `bench/**`.

"""Terminal-Bench adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Follows the AbstractInstalledAgent pattern (same as the claude-code agent):
a setup script installs fa inside the task container, and the agent runs as
`fa -p "<instruction>"` in the container's tmux session, so fa's bash/read/
write tools operate on the container filesystem.

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah + lib/),
                         extracted to /opt/fa by the setup script.
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64) — the object may
                         also declare the optional capability pair
                         "contextWindow"/"maxTokens" (gh-1471 D4: bench's
                         kimi mapping pins 200000/16384 so a catalog drift
                         can never silently truncate the served window;
                         absent fields keep the catalog defaults).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122, see bench/fa_agent_timeout.py): when any
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER is set, perform_task takes over the outer
  agent deadline from the harness's flat wait_for: the agent runs under a
  progress-aware ladder (silent => die at the base cap as today; output
  flowing => deadline recedes up to the hard ceiling). With no knobs set
  this module delegates to the stock AbstractInstalledAgent.perform_task
  byte-for-byte (historical comparability, issue #1122 REG-1).

  Round 3 (issue #1392): when FA_STALL_GAP_SEC or
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC activates the progress-watch mode, the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch (progressing trials die
  only at the absolute ceiling; a >= stall-gap gap is a provable stall).
  Every trial also gets: live per-request lines as they happen
  (LiveProgress over the pane's FA_CONN events), a per-trial
  bench_metrics.json (latency p50/p95, watchdog fires, fresh-vs-reused),
  a hang-*.json forensics dump on a stall verdict BEFORE the kill lands
  (StallSentinel), and an export-guard.json row when the agent produced
  output but the session export came back empty (ExportGuard).

  gh-1430 — the ordering invariant this adapter operates under:

      fa's watchdog is the sole arbiter of stream death; the bench gap
      only catches pane/process death.

  fa errors a truly dead provider stream itself at
  providerStreamIdleTimeout (300s, lib/src/providers/provider_common.dart)
  and, since gh-1430, heartbeats `… reasoning Ns (streaming)` to the pane
  while its stream emits events the headless output mode does not render.
  The shipped stall gap (360s = watchdog + margin, bench/fa_agent_timeout.py)
  therefore fires only when the PANE went silent — process death or a
  wedged pane — never while fa itself considers the stream live. The REG
  in test_fa_agent_timeout.py pins the gap >= watchdog against the Dart
  source and fails if either side drifts.

  Issue #1406 (never-again): the launch line itself carries the
  non-secret FA_CONN_* env into the tmux pane (`export …; env |
  grep FA_CONN > /tmp/fa-conn-env.txt;` prefix — pane env belongs to the
  shell/server history, not to the step env that typed a later command),
  the capture folds into agent-logs/fa-conn-env.txt as runtime proof,
  and the loud-empty guard fires (conn-guard.json + a ::warning::
  annotation) when a trial's bench_metrics.json has requests == []
  despite real usage tokens — an instrumentation outage is never silent.

  PYTHONPATH=bench/terminal_bench tb run -d terminal-bench-core==0.1.1 \
    --agent-import-path fa_agent:FaAgent -t hello-world

name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `test_other_failure_modes_stay_raw_in_the_stock_audit` fails on main with `FileNotFoundError: …/fa-agent-timeout.json` (bench-harbor setup job red since the Oct-14 wave), plus dozens of `session usage extraction failed` / `fa session export failed` warnings polluting the same log, plus a stale REG red in `bench/mls_bench`.

   ```python

       return result
   ```
   early-returns BEFORE the gh-1576 (I2) audit write. `_NEVER_STARTED_MODES = {AGENT_INSTALLATION_FAILED, UNKNOWN_AGENT_ERROR}`, so with a known external cap the audit file is never written for exactly the "other failure modes" the gh-1576 contract says must land **raw** — the `else str(result.failure_mode.value)` branch of the same audit call is dead code for those modes. The writer's own comment ("with an external cap known, even this unsupervised termination lands the audit") states the contract the early return violates. Reproduced locally with CI parity: `python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench` → `Ran 410 tests … FAILED (errors=1)`, same FileNotFoundError.

2. **Unfaithful docker fakes (AC2)** — `FakeTmuxSession.container` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`) and `FakeContainer` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_progress_watch_adapter.py`) return `types.SimpleNamespace(exit_code=…, output=…)` from `exec_run`, but docker-py's `ExecResult` is a **namedtuple** `(exit_code, output)`: production unpacks it in `_fold_session_usage` (`exit_code, output = …exec_run(…)` → "cannot unpack non-iterable types.SimpleNamespace") while reading attributes elsewhere. Both fakes also lack `get_archive` (the issue #1339 session export calls `session.container.get_archive` → "'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'get_archive'"). Not a production regression: the production call shapes match the real docker API; the fakes predate the #1339 export and the fold's unpack. ~18 warning pairs across otherwise-passing tests.

"""Terminal-Bench adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Follows the AbstractInstalledAgent pattern (same as the claude-code agent):
a setup script installs fa inside the task container, and the agent runs as
`fa -p "<instruction>"` in the container's tmux session, so fa's bash/read/
write tools operate on the container filesystem.

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah + lib/),
                         extracted to /opt/fa by the setup script.
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64) — the object may
                         also declare the optional capability pair
                         "contextWindow"/"maxTokens" (gh-1471 D4: bench's
                         kimi mapping pins 200000/16384 so a catalog drift
                         can never silently truncate the served window;
                         absent fields keep the catalog defaults).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122, see bench/fa_agent_timeout.py): when any
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER is set, perform_task takes over the outer
  agent deadline from the harness's flat wait_for: the agent runs under a
  progress-aware ladder (silent => die at the base cap as today; output
  flowing => deadline recedes up to the hard ceiling). With no knobs set
  this module delegates to the stock AbstractInstalledAgent.perform_task
  byte-for-byte (historical comparability, issue #1122 REG-1).

  Round 3 (issue #1392): when FA_STALL_GAP_SEC or
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC activates the progress-watch mode, the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch (progressing trials die
  only at the absolute ceiling; a >= stall-gap gap is a provable stall).
  Every trial also gets: live per-request lines as they happen
  (LiveProgress over the pane's FA_CONN events), a per-trial
  bench_metrics.json (latency p50/p95, watchdog fires, fresh-vs-reused),
  a hang-*.json forensics dump on a stall verdict BEFORE the kill lands
  (StallSentinel), and an export-guard.json row when the agent produced
  output but the session export came back empty (ExportGuard).

  gh-1430 — the ordering invariant this adapter operates under:

      fa's watchdog is the sole arbiter of stream death; the bench gap
      only catches pane/process death.

  fa errors a truly dead provider stream itself at
  providerStreamIdleTimeout (300s, lib/src/providers/provider_common.dart)
  and, since gh-1430, heartbeats `… reasoning Ns (streaming)` to the pane
  while its stream emits events the headless output mode does not render.
  The shipped stall gap (360s = watchdog + margin, bench/fa_agent_timeout.py)
  therefore fires only when the PANE went silent — process death or a
  wedged pane — never while fa itself considers the stream live. The REG
  in test_fa_agent_timeout.py pins the gap >= watchdog against the Dart
  source and fails if either side drifts.

  Issue #1406 (never-again): the launch line itself carries the
  non-secret FA_CONN_* env into the tmux pane (`export …; env |
  grep FA_CONN > /tmp/fa-conn-env.txt;` prefix — pane env belongs to the
  shell/server history, not to the step env that typed a later command),
  the capture folds into agent-logs/fa-conn-env.txt as runtime proof,
  and the loud-empty guard fires (conn-guard.json + a ::warning::
  annotation) when a trial's bench_metrics.json has requests == []
  despite real usage tokens — an instrumentation outage is never silent.

  PYTHONPATH=bench/terminal_bench tb run -d terminal-bench-core==0.1.1 \
    --agent-import-path fa_agent:FaAgent -t hello-world

        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1638

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `test_other_failure_modes_stay_raw_in_the_stock_audit` fails on main with `FileNotFoundError: …/fa-agent-timeout.json` (bench-harbor setup job red since the Oct-14 wave), plus dozens of `session usage extraction failed` / `fa session export failed` warnings polluting the same log, plus a stale REG red in `bench/mls_bench`.

**Root cause** (three independent rots, all in `bench/`):

1. **Audit writer gap (AC1)** — `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py`, `FaAgent.perform_task`, stock/unsupervised path. The gh-1209 never-started guard
   ```python
   if result.failure_mode in _NEVER_STARTED_MODES:
       return result
   ```
   early-returns BEFORE the gh-1576 (I2) audit write. `_NEVER_STARTED_MODES = {AGENT_INSTALLATION_FAILED, UNKNOWN_AGENT_ERROR}`, so with a known external cap the audit file is never written for exactly the "other failure modes" the gh-1576 contract says must land **raw** — the `else str(result.failure_mode.value)` branch of the same audit call is dead code for those modes. The writer's own comment ("with an external cap known, even this unsupervised termination lands the audit") states the contract the early return violates. Reproduced locally with CI parity: `python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench` → `Ran 410 tests … FAILED (errors=1)`, same FileNotFoundError.

2. **Unfaithful docker fakes (AC2)** — `FakeTmuxSession.container` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`) and `FakeContainer` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_progress_watch_adapter.py`) return `types.SimpleNamespace(exit_code=…, output=…)` from `exec_run`, but docker-py's `ExecResult` is a **namedtuple** `(exit_code, output)`: production unpacks it in `_fold_session_usage` (`exit_code, output = …exec_run(…)` → "cannot unpack non-iterable types.SimpleNamespace") while reading attributes elsewhere. Both fakes also lack `get_archive` (the issue #1339 session export calls `session.container.get_archive` → "'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'get_archive'"). Not a production regression: the production call shapes match the real docker API; the fakes predate the #1339 export and the fold's unpack. ~18 warning pairs across otherwise-passing tests.

3. **Stale REG in the third bench root (AC4 blocker)** — `bench/mls_bench/test_build_run.py::RegressionPinsTest::test_bench_harbor_family_anchors` pins the pre-#1316 default dataset literal `terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0`; #1316 deliberately moved the bench-harbor default to `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest`. """Terminal-Bench adapter for the `fa` coding agent (flutter_agent_harness).

Follows the AbstractInstalledAgent pattern (same as the claude-code agent):
a setup script installs fa inside the task container, and the agent runs as
`fa -p "<instruction>"` in the container's tmux session, so fa's bash/read/
write tools operate on the container filesystem.

Host-side inputs (environment):
  FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL      tar.gz of a `dart build cli` bundle (bin/fah + lib/),
                         extracted to /opt/fa by the setup script.
  FA_PROVIDER_TYPE       provider kind (default: anthropic).
  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG     JSON {"baseUrl": ..., "model": ..., "apiKeyEnvVar": ...}
                         (or FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64) — the object may
                         also declare the optional capability pair
                         "contextWindow"/"maxTokens" (gh-1471 D4: bench's
                         kimi mapping pins 200000/16384 so a catalog drift
                         can never silently truncate the served window;
                         absent fields keep the catalog defaults).
  <apiKeyEnvVar>         the API key itself, e.g. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

  Timeout knobs (issue #1122, see bench/fa_agent_timeout.py): when any
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC / FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION / FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC /
  FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER is set, perform_task takes over the outer
  agent deadline from the harness's flat wait_for: the agent runs under a
  progress-aware ladder (silent => die at the base cap as today; output
  flowing => deadline recedes up to the hard ceiling). With no knobs set
  this module delegates to the stock AbstractInstalledAgent.perform_task
  byte-for-byte (historical comparability, issue #1122 REG-1).

  Round 3 (issue #1392): when FA_STALL_GAP_SEC or
  FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC activates the progress-watch mode, the
  kill decision is the gap-aware ProgressWatch (progressing trials die
  only at the absolute ceiling; a >= stall-gap gap is a provable stall).
  Every trial also gets: live per-request lines as they happen
  (LiveProgress over the pane's FA_CONN events), a per-trial
  bench_metrics.json (latency p50/p95, watchdog fires, fresh-vs-reused),
  a hang-*.json forensics dump on a stall verdict BEFORE the kill lands
  (StallSentinel), and an export-guard.json row when the agent produced
  output but the session export came back empty (ExportGuard).

  gh-1430 — the ordering invariant this adapter operates under:

      fa's watchdog is the sole arbiter of stream death; the bench gap
      only catches pane/process death.

  fa errors a truly dead provider stream itself at
  providerStreamIdleTimeout (300s, lib/src/providers/provider_common.dart)
  and, since gh-1430, heartbeats `… reasoning Ns (streaming)` to the pane
  while its stream emits events the headless output mode does not render.
  The shipped stall gap (360s = watchdog + margin, bench/fa_agent_timeout.py)
  therefore fires only when the PANE went silent — process death or a
  wedged pane — never while fa itself considers the stream live. The REG
  in test_fa_agent_timeout.py pins the gap >= watchdog against the Dart
  source and fails if either side drifts.

  Issue #1406 (never-again): the launch line itself carries the
  non-secret FA_CONN_* env into the tmux pane (`export …; env |
  grep FA_CONN > /tmp/fa-conn-env.txt;` prefix — pane env belongs to the

name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `test_other_failure_modes_stay_raw_in_the_stock_audit` fails on main with `FileNotFoundError: …/fa-agent-timeout.json` (bench-harbor setup job red since the Oct-14 wave), plus dozens of `session usage extraction failed` / `fa session export failed` warnings polluting the same log, plus a stale REG red in `bench/mls_bench`.

**Root cause** (three independent rots, all in `bench/`):

1. **Audit writer gap (AC1)** — `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py`, `FaAgent.perform_task`, stock/unsupervised path. The gh-1209 never-started guard
   ```python
   if result.failure_mode in _NEVER_STARTED_MODES:
       return result
   ```
   early-returns BEFORE the gh-1576 (I2) audit write. `_NEVER_STARTED_MODES = {AGENT_INSTALLATION_FAILED, UNKNOWN_AGENT_ERROR}`, so with a known external cap the audit file is never written for exactly the "other failure modes" the gh-1576 contract says must land **raw** — the `else str(result.failure_mode.value)` branch of the same audit call is dead code for those modes. The writer's own comment ("with an external cap known, even this unsupervised termination lands the audit") states the contract the early return violates. Reproduced locally with CI parity: `python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench` → `Ran 410 tests … FAILED (errors=1)`, same FileNotFoundError.

2. **Unfaithful docker fakes (AC2)** — `FakeTmuxSession.container` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`) and `FakeContainer` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_progress_watch_adapter.py`) return `types.SimpleNamespace(exit_code=…, output=…)` from `exec_run`, but docker-py's `ExecResult` is a **namedtuple** `(exit_code, output)`: production unpacks it in `_fold_session_usage` (`exit_code, output = …exec_run(…)` → "cannot unpack non-iterable types.SimpleNamespace") while reading attributes elsewhere. Both fakes also lack `get_archive` (the issue #1339 session export calls `session.container.get_archive` → "'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'get_archive'"). Not a production regression: the production call shapes match the real docker API; the fakes predate the #1339 export and the fold's unpack. ~18 warning pairs across otherwise-passing tests.

3. **Stale REG in the third bench root (AC4 blocker)** — `bench/mls_bench/test_build_run.py::RegressionPinsTest::test_bench_harbor_family_anchors` pins the pre-#1316 default dataset literal `terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0`; #1316 deliberately moved the bench-harbor default to `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest`. Same rot class as the ticket's systemic lesson: mls_bench is only executed by bench-mls.yml's dispatch-gated setup, so the drift sat invisible.

**Impact**: every bench-harbor/bench dispatch dies at setup (`errors=1`) — shards never start; the warnings bury real signal in trial logs; any PR touching bench/ ships untested python.

**Fix approach**:
1. Skip only the usage fold for never-started modes; keep the gh-1576 audit write (the raw failure-mode string IS the truthful outcome). Parity with the harbor adapter holds (harbor always writes the audit on every termination path).
2. Make both fakes faithful to docker-py: namedtuple `ExecResult` (unpack + attribute access both work) and a `get_archive` returning `([valid_tar], stat)`.
3. Update the stale REG to pin the shipped #1316 default (2.1), keeping the agent/MLS-free anchors.
4. Systemic guard: new path-filtered workflow `.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml` running the exact setup gate (same pinned deps: `harbor[modal]==0.23.0`, `terminal-bench==0.2.18`, python 3.13) on every PR and main push touching `bench/**`.

def _importable(name: str) -> bool:
    # find_spec is not enough: with bench/terminal_bench on sys.path (as
    # unittest discover does), find_spec("terminal_bench") matches the
    # DIRECTORY itself as a namespace package and false-positives.
    try:
        module = importlib.import_module(name)
    except ImportError:
        return False
    # test_progress_watch_adapter installs a stdlib stub package under the
    # same name (so its ITs run where terminal-bench is not installed);
    # a stub is not the real dependency.
    return not getattr(module, "__fa_tb_stub__", False)


TB_AVAILABLE = _importable("terminal_bench.agents.base_agent")
HARBOR_AVAILABLE = _importable("harbor")

KNOB_NAMES = (
    "FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC",
    "FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION",
    "FA_AGENT_IDLE_WINDOW_SEC",
    "FA_AGENT_CEILING_MULTIPLIER",
)

# gh-1576: the external harness cap rides its own env var; every clean-env
# helper must strip it so a host-exported cap cannot leak into a test that
# means to pin the no-cap byte-identity.
EXTERNAL_CAP_NAME = "FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC"


def clean_env(**overrides):
    env = {
        name: value
        for name, value in os.environ.items()
        if name not in KNOB_NAMES + (EXTERNAL_CAP_NAME,)
    }
    env.update(overrides)
    return env


def _dart_duration_seconds(declaration: str) -> float:
    """Seconds inside a Dart `Duration(...)` constructor call.

    Accepts any argument subset/order (`Duration(seconds: 180)`,
    `Duration(minutes: 5)`, `Duration(minutes: 1, seconds: 30)`,
    `Duration(milliseconds: 500)`) — the coupling REG (gh-1430) feeds it
    the `providerStreamIdleTimeout` line from the Dart source, and the
    parse must survive a benign unit change there.
    """

# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1638

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `test_other_failure_modes_stay_raw_in_the_stock_audit` fails on main with `FileNotFoundError: …/fa-agent-timeout.json` (bench-harbor setup job red since the Oct-14 wave), plus dozens of `session usage extraction failed` / `fa session export failed` warnings polluting the same log, plus a stale REG red in `bench/mls_bench`.

**Root cause** (three independent rots, all in `bench/`):

1. **Audit writer gap (AC1)** — `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py`, `FaAgent.perform_task`, stock/unsupervised path. The gh-1209 never-started guard
   ```python
   if result.failure_mode in _NEVER_STARTED_MODES:
       return result
   ```
   early-returns BEFORE the gh-1576 (I2) audit write. `_NEVER_STARTED_MODES = {AGENT_INSTALLATION_FAILED, UNKNOWN_AGENT_ERROR}`, so with a known external cap the audit file is never written for exactly the "other failure modes" the gh-1576 contract says must land **raw** — the `else str(result.failure_mode.value)` branch of the same audit call is dead code for those modes. The writer's own comment ("with an external cap known, even this unsupervised termination lands the audit") states the contract the early return violates. Reproduced locally with CI parity: `python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench` → `Ran 410 tests … FAILED (errors=1)`, same FileNotFoundError.

2. **Unfaithful docker fakes (AC2)** — `FakeTmuxSession.container` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`) and `FakeContainer` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_progress_watch_adapter.py`) return `types.SimpleNamespace(exit_code=…, output=…)` from `exec_run`, but docker-py's `ExecResult` is a **namedtuple** `(exit_code, output)`: production unpacks it in `_fold_session_usage` (`exit_code, output = …exec_run(…)` → "cannot unpack non-iterable types.SimpleNamespace") while reading attributes elsewhere. Both fakes also lack `get_archive` (the issue #1339 session export calls `session.container.get_archive` → "'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'get_archive'"). Not a production regression: the production call shapes match the real docker API; the fakes predate the #1339 export and the fold's unpack. ~18 warning pairs across otherwise-passing tests.

3. **Stale REG in the third bench root (AC4 blocker)** — `bench/mls_bench/test_build_run.py::RegressionPinsTest::test_bench_harbor_family_anchors` pins the pre-#1316 default dataset literal `terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0`; #1316 deliberately moved the bench-harbor default to `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest`. Same rot class as the ticket's systemic lesson: mls_bench is only executed by bench-mls.yml's dispatch-gated setup, so the drift sat invisible.

**Impact**: every bench-harbor/bench dispatch dies at setup (`errors=1`) — shards never start; the warnings bury real signal in trial logs; any PR touching bench/ ships untested python.

**Fix approach**:
1. Skip only the usage fold for never-started modes; keep the gh-1576 audit write (the raw failure-mode string IS the truthful outcome). Parity with the harbor adapter holds (harbor always writes the audit on every termination path).
2. Make both fakes faithful to docker-py: namedtuple `ExecResult` (unpack + attribute access both work) and a `get_archive` returning `([valid_tar], stat)`.
3. Update the stale REG to pin the shipped #1316 default (2.1), keeping the agent/MLS-free anchors.
4. Systemic guard: new path-filtered workflow `.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml` running the exact setup gate (same pinned deps: `harbor[modal]==0.23.0`, `terminal-bench==0.2.18`, python 3.13) on every PR and main push touching `bench/**`.
