# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issue #147). The `dataset` input takes a
# family label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or a full Harbor dataset id — resolved
# and validated by bench/harbor_fa/families.py (unknown or version-less
# specs fail fast; never a silent fallback). The default dispatch is the
# 2.1 family (issue #1316: the bench migrates to Terminal-Bench 2.x /
# Harbor — supersedes #1124 AC4's 4.0 default; 4.0/3.0/2.0 stay one input
# away). CPU shards run the default Harbor `docker` sandbox on
# ubuntu-latest (GH runners ship docker — no Modal/cloud dependency for
# the default dispatch, #1316); GPU tasks always route to a modal shard
# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.
# Results upload
# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + an env-provider-preconfig, secrets env-only and never echoed
# (keys pass base64-encoded into the task container; CI masks both raw
# and base64 forms).
#
# gh-1503: the provider is no longer a z.ai hardcode — the dispatch
# picks zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to the pre-gh-1503
# wiring), kimi-for-coding (model id == plan name; FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY), or
# `custom`
# (provider-config JSON validated in the resolve step; key only from
# FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY). The setup job's resolve step is a byte-consistent
# copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 step — keep both in sync (cross-reference
# comment in both files). With the z.ai budget at zero, the kimi path is
# what keeps this workflow dispatchable.
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY      — kimi coding key for kimi-for-coding (the model
#                            id is the plan name; shared with bench.yml;
#                            never the review factory's KIMI_REVIEW_KEY)
#   FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY    — key for provider=custom, injected as FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

run-name: fa bench-harbor · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1503, same contract as bench.yml gh-1471: default = pre-gh-1503 behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1503 (bench.yml gh-1471 D1/AC 2a): ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Terminal-Bench family: label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or full Harbor id (see bench/harbor_fa/families.py); default 2.1 (issue #1316)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      attempts:
        description: 'harbor --n-attempts per trial (-k)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      n-concurrent:
        description: 'harbor --n-concurrent trials (1 = z.ai rate-limit safe; the kimi coding plan tolerates more — owner picks at dispatch)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count for CPU tasks (~4 tasks/shard keeps each job under the 6h window)'
        required: false
        default: '16'
      cpu-env:
        description: 'Harbor env for CPU shards (docker default — issue #1316; modal for the self-hosted path)'
        required: false
        default: 'docker'
      cpu-runner:
        description: 'Runner label hosting the harbor CLI (ubuntu-latest default — GH runners ship docker; self-hosted for the modal path)'
        required: false
        default: 'ubuntu-latest'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared task caps)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds the runner for hours; queue a second dispatch
# instead of stacking them. One group across the whole family: harbor
# runs serialize even when different dataset versions are dispatched
# back-to-back.
concurrency:
  group: bench-harbor
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & shard dataset
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      cpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.cpu_count }}
      gpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.gpu_count }}
      family: ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }}
      dataset: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # gh-1503: byte-consistent copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 resolve step
      # (same run block, same outputs) — the single-source extraction was
      # rejected there to keep the workflow self-contained; the
      # cross-reference comment in both files is the sync contract. Maps
      # the provider choice to the full provider triple (type/baseUrl/

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `test_other_failure_modes_stay_raw_in_the_stock_audit` fails on main with `FileNotFoundError: …/fa-agent-timeout.json` (bench-harbor setup job red since the Oct-14 wave), plus dozens of `session usage extraction failed` / `fa session export failed` warnings polluting the same log, plus a stale REG red in `bench/mls_bench`.

**Root cause** (three independent rots, all in `bench/`):

1. **Audit writer gap (AC1)** — `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py`, `FaAgent.perform_task`, stock/unsupervised path. The gh-1209 never-started guard
   ```python
   if result.failure_mode in _NEVER_STARTED_MODES:
       return result
   ```
   early-returns BEFORE the gh-1576 (I2) audit write. `_NEVER_STARTED_MODES = {AGENT_INSTALLATION_FAILED, UNKNOWN_AGENT_ERROR}`, so with a known external cap the audit file is never written for exactly the "other failure modes" the gh-1576 contract says must land **raw** — the `else str(result.failure_mode.value)` branch of the same audit call is dead code for those modes. The writer's own comment ("with an external cap known, even this unsupervised termination lands the audit") states the contract the early return violates. Reproduced locally with CI parity: `python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench` → `Ran 410 tests … FAILED (errors=1)`, same FileNotFoundError.

2. **Unfaithful docker fakes (AC2)** — `FakeTmuxSession.container` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`) and `FakeContainer` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_progress_watch_adapter.py`) return `types.SimpleNamespace(exit_code=…, output=…)` from `exec_run`, but docker-py's `ExecResult` is a **namedtuple** `(exit_code, output)`: production unpacks it in `_fold_session_usage` (`exit_code, output = …exec_run(…)` → "cannot unpack non-iterable types.SimpleNamespace") while reading attributes elsewhere. Both fakes also lack `get_archive` (the issue #1339 session export calls `session.container.get_archive` → "'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'get_archive'"). Not a production regression: the production call shapes match the real docker API; the fakes predate the #1339 export and the fold's unpack. ~18 warning pairs across otherwise-passing tests.

3. **Stale REG in the third bench root (AC4 blocker)** — `bench/mls_bench/test_build_run.py::RegressionPinsTest::test_bench_harbor_family_anchors` pins the pre-#1316 default dataset literal `terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0`; #1316 deliberately moved the bench-harbor default to `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest`. Same rot class as the ticket's systemic lesson: mls_bench is only executed by bench-mls.yml's dispatch-gated setup, so the drift sat invisible.

**Impact**: every bench-harbor/bench dispatch dies at setup (`errors=1`) — shards never start; the warnings bury real signal in trial logs; any PR touching bench/ ships untested python.

**Fix approach**:
1. Skip only the usage fold for never-started modes; keep the gh-1576 audit write (the raw failure-mode string IS the truthful outcome). Parity with the harbor adapter holds (harbor always writes the audit on every termination path).
2. Make both fakes faithful to docker-py: namedtuple `ExecResult` (unpack + attribute access both work) and a `get_archive` returning `([valid_tar], stat)`.
3. Update the stale REG to pin the shipped #1316 default (2.1), keeping the agent/MLS-free anchors.
4. Systemic guard: new path-filtered workflow `.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml` running the exact setup gate (same pinned deps: `harbor[modal]==0.23.0`, `terminal-bench==0.2.18`, python 3.13) on every PR and main push touching `bench/**`.

{"content":"# gh-1638 AC4 (the systemic lesson): the bench-script python tests ran
# ONLY inside the bench workflows' setup jobs (dispatch-gated), so the
# Oct-14 merge wave rotted them on main invisibly for 3+ days — every
# dispatch died at setup while the main quality gate (dart test / coverage
# / guards) never executes a line of python. This job runs the EXACT setup
# gate (same discovery roots, same pinned deps) on every bench/** change:
# a red bench-script test now fails the PR and main cannot rot silently.
name: Bench script tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Superseded PR runs die instantly; main-push runs are never cancelled
# mid-flight (same release-protection principle as ci.yml).
concurrency:
  group: Bench script tests-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal permissions.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  unit-tests:
    name: Unit-test bench scripts
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # terminal-bench-era note (bench-harbor.yml): harbor is fine on 3.13;
      # typer-based CLIs break on 3.14.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned exactly like the bench workflows' setup gate: the adapters
      # target the harbor 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent / terminal-bench 0.2.18
      # import surfaces.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0' 'terminal-bench==0.2.18'

      # Same gate as bench.yml / bench-harbor.yml "Unit-test bench scripts"
      # (plus the bench-mls.yml root — all three bench discovery roots);
      # keep the step bodies in sync with those workflows.
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
        run: |
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/mls_bench -v
","path":".github/workflows/bench-tests.yml"}

Critical discovery: most `exec_run` consumers use **attribute access** (`result.exit_code`, `result.output`), while only `_fold_session_usage` (line 793) uses **tuple unpacking** (`exit_code, output = ...`).

Real docker `exec_run` returns an `ExecResult` namedtuple — `(exit_code, output)` — which supports BOTH tuple unpacking AND attribute access. So both shapes work against real docker.

The fake returns SimpleNamespace → attribute access works (the supervised tests pass), but tuple unpacking fails (the fold warning).

So the faithful fake shape is a **namedtuple** `(exit_code, output)` — like docker's ExecResult: attribute access AND unpacking both work. That's the cleanest fix: use `collections.namedtuple`-style return in `_exec_run`.

For `get_archive`: real docker returns `(bits, stat)` tuple. Production: `bits, _ = session.container.get_archive(...)`. Fake must return that tuple shape.

            FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG="{}",

1. **Audit writer gap (AC1)** — `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py`, `FaAgent.perform_task`, stock/unsupervised path. The gh-1209 never-started guard
   ```python
   if result.failure_mode in _NEVER_STARTED_MODES:
       return result
   ```
   early-returns BEFORE the gh-1576 (I2) audit write. `_NEVER_STARTED_MODES = {AGENT_INSTALLATION_FAILED, UNKNOWN_AGENT_ERROR}`, so with a known external cap the audit file is never written for exactly the "other failure modes" the gh-1576 contract says must land **raw** — the `else str(result.failure_mode.value)` branch of the same audit call is dead code for those modes. The writer's own comment ("with an external cap known, even this unsupervised termination lands the audit") states the contract the early return violates. Reproduced locally with CI parity: `python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench` → `Ran 410 tests … FAILED (errors=1)`, same FileNotFoundError.

2. **Unfaithful docker fakes (AC2)** — `FakeTmuxSession.container` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`) and `FakeContainer` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_progress_watch_adapter.py`) return `types.SimpleNamespace(exit_code=…, output=…)` from `exec_run`, but docker-py's `ExecResult` is a **namedtuple** `(exit_code, output)`: production unpacks it in `_fold_session_usage` (`exit_code, output = …exec_run(…)` → "cannot unpack non-iterable types.SimpleNamespace") while reading attributes elsewhere. Both fakes also lack `get_archive` (the issue #1339 session export calls `session.container.get_archive` → "'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'get_archive'"). Not a production regression: the production call shapes match the real docker API; the fakes predate the #1339 export and the fold's unpack. ~18 warning pairs across otherwise-passing tests.

3. **Stale REG in the third bench root (AC4 blocker)** — `bench/mls_bench/test_build_run.py::RegressionPinsTest::test_bench_harbor_family_anchors` pins the pre-#1316 default dataset literal `terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0`; #1316 deliberately moved the bench-harbor default to `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest`. Same rot class as the ticket's systemic lesson: mls_bench is only executed by bench-mls.yml's dispatch-gated setup, so the drift sat invisible.

**Impact**: every bench-harbor/bench dispatch dies at setup (`errors=1`) — shards never start; the warnings bury real signal in trial logs; any PR touching bench/ ships untested python.

**Fix approach**:
1. Skip only the usage fold for never-started modes; keep the gh-1576 audit write (the raw failure-mode string IS the truthful outcome). Parity with the harbor adapter holds (harbor always writes the audit on every termination path).
2. Make both fakes faithful to docker-py: namedtuple `ExecResult` (unpack + attribute access both work) and a `get_archive` returning `([valid_tar], stat)`.
3. Update the stale REG to pin the shipped #1316 default (2.1), keeping the agent/MLS-free anchors.
4. Systemic guard: new path-filtered workflow `.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml` running the exact setup gate (same pinned deps: `harbor[modal]==0.23.0`, `terminal-bench==0.2.18`, python 3.13) on every PR and main push touching `bench/**`.

{"content":"# gh-1638 AC4 (the systemic lesson): the bench-script python tests ran
# ONLY inside the bench workflows' setup jobs (dispatch-gated), so the
# Oct-14 merge wave rotted them on main invisibly for 3+ days — every
# dispatch died at setup while the main quality gate (dart test / coverage
# / guards) never executes a line of python. This job runs the EXACT setup
# gate (same discovery roots, same pinned deps) on every bench/** change:
# a red bench-script test now fails the PR and main cannot rot silently.
name: Bench script tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Superseded PR runs die instantly; main-push runs are never cancelled
# mid-flight (same release-protection principle as ci.yml).
concurrency:
  group: Bench script tests-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal permissions.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  unit-tests:
    name: Unit-test bench scripts
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # typer-based CLIs break on 3.14.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0

          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned exactly like the bench workflows' setup gate: the adapters
      # target the harbor 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent / terminal-bench 0.2.18
      # import surfaces.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0' 'terminal-bench==0.2.18'

      # Same gate as bench.yml / bench-harbor.yml "Unit-test bench scripts"
      # (plus the bench-mls.yml root — all three bench discovery roots);
      # keep the step bodies in sync with those workflows.
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
        run: |
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/mls_bench -v

blocks.text:
# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1638

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `test_other_failure_modes_stay_raw_in_the_stock_audit` fails on main with `FileNotFoundError: …/fa-agent-timeout.json` (bench-harbor setup job red since the Oct-14 wave), plus dozens of `session usage extraction failed` / `fa session export failed` warnings polluting the same log, plus a stale REG red in `bench/mls_bench`.

**Root cause** (three independent rots, all in `bench/`):

1. **Audit writer gap (AC1)** — `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py`, `FaAgent.perform_task`, stock/unsupervised path. The gh-1209 never-started guard
   ```python
   if result.failure_mode in _NEVER_STARTED_MODES:
       return result
   ```
   early-returns BEFORE the gh-1576 (I2) audit write. `_NEVER_STARTED_MODES = {AGENT_INSTALLATION_FAILED, UNKNOWN_AGENT_ERROR}`, so with a known external cap the audit file is never written for exactly the "other failure modes" the gh-1576 contract says must land **raw** — the `else str(result.failure_mode.value)` branch of the same audit call is dead code for those modes. The writer's own comment ("with an external cap known, even this unsupervised termination lands the audit") states the contract the early return violates. Reproduced locally with CI parity: `python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench` → `Ran 410 tests … FAILED (errors=1)`, same FileNotFoundError.

2. **Unfaithful docker fakes (AC2)** — `FakeTmuxSession.container` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`) and `FakeContainer` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_progress_watch_adapter.py`) return `types.SimpleNamespace(exit_code=…, output=…)` from `exec_run`, but docker-py's `ExecResult` is a **namedtuple** `(exit_code, output)`: production unpacks it in `_fold_session_usage` (`exit_code, output = …exec_run(…)` → "cannot unpack non-iterable types.SimpleNamespace") while reading attributes elsewhere. Both fakes also lack `get_archive` (the issue #1339 session export calls `session.container.get_archive` → "'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'get_archive'"). Not a production regression: the production call shapes match the real docker API; the fakes predate the #1339 export and the fold's unpack. ~18 warning pairs across otherwise-passing tests.

3. **Stale REG in the third bench root (AC4 blocker)** — `bench/mls_bench/test_build_run.py::RegressionPinsTest::test_bench_harbor_family_anchors` pins the pre-#1316 default dataset literal `terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0`; #1316 deliberately moved the bench-harbor default to `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest`. Same rot class as the ticket's systemic lesson: mls_bench is only executed by bench-mls.yml's dispatch-gated setup, so the drift sat invisible.

**Impact**: every bench-harbor/bench dispatch dies at setup (`errors=1`) — shards never start; the warnings bury real signal in trial logs; any PR touching bench/ ships untested python.

**Fix approach**:
1. Skip only the usage fold for never-started modes; keep the gh-1576 audit write (the raw failure-mode string IS the truthful outcome). Parity with the harbor adapter holds (harbor always writes the audit on every termination path).
2. Make both fakes faithful to docker-py: namedtuple `ExecResult` (unpack + attribute access both work) and a `get_archive` returning `([valid_tar], stat)`.
3. Update the stale REG to pin the shipped #1316 default (2.1), keeping the agent/MLS-free anchors.
4. Systemic guard: new path-filtered workflow `.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml` running the exact setup gate (same pinned deps: `harbor[modal]==0.23.0`, `terminal-bench==0.2.18`, python 3.13) on every PR and main push touching `bench/**`.

**Previous attempt**: none (first fix for gh-1638).

{"content":"# gh-1638 AC4 (the systemic lesson): the bench-script python tests ran
# ONLY inside the bench workflows' setup jobs (dispatch-gated), so the
# Oct-14 merge wave rotted them on main invisibly for 3+ days — every
# dispatch died at setup while the main quality gate (dart test / coverage
# / guards) never executes a line of python. This job runs the EXACT setup
# gate (same discovery roots, same pinned deps) on every bench/** change:
# a red bench-script test now fails the PR and main cannot rot silently.
name: Bench script tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Superseded PR runs die instantly; main-push runs are never cancelled
# mid-flight (same release-protection principle as ci.yml).
concurrency:
  group: Bench script tests-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal permissions.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  unit-tests:
    name: Unit-test bench scripts
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # terminal-bench-era note (bench-harbor.yml): harbor is fine on 3.13;
      # typer-based CLIs break on 3.14.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned exactly like the bench workflows' setup gate: the adapters
      # target the harbor 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent / terminal-bench 0.2.18
      # import surfaces.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0' 'terminal-bench==0.2.18'

      # Same gate as bench.yml / bench-harbor.yml "Unit-test bench scripts"
      # (plus the bench-mls.yml root — all three bench discovery roots);
      # keep the step bodies in sync with those workflows.
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
        run: |
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/mls_bench -v

on:

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1638

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `test_other_failure_modes_stay_raw_in_the_stock_audit` fails on main with `FileNotFoundError: …/fa-agent-timeout.json` (bench-harbor setup job red since the Oct-14 wave), plus dozens of `session usage extraction failed` / `fa session export failed` warnings polluting the same log, plus a stale REG red in `bench/mls_bench`.

**Root cause** (three independent rots, all in `bench/`):

1. **Audit writer gap (AC1)** — `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py`, `FaAgent.perform_task`, stock/unsupervised path. The gh-1209 never-started guard
   ```python
   if result.failure_mode in _NEVER_STARTED_MODES:
       return result
   ```
   early-returns BEFORE the gh-1576 (I2) audit write. `_NEVER_STARTED_MODES = {AGENT_INSTALLATION_FAILED, UNKNOWN_AGENT_ERROR}`, so with a known external cap the audit file is never written for exactly the "other failure modes" the gh-1576 contract says must land **raw** — the `else str(result.failure_mode.value)` branch of the same audit call is dead code for those modes. The writer's own comment ("with an external cap known, even this unsupervised termination lands the audit") states the contract the early return violates. Reproduced locally with CI parity: `python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench` → `Ran 410 tests … FAILED (errors=1)`, same FileNotFoundError.

2. **Unfaithful docker fakes (AC2)** — `FakeTmuxSession.container` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`) and `FakeContainer` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_progress_watch_adapter.py`) return `types.SimpleNamespace(exit_code=…, output=…)` from `exec_run`, but docker-py's `ExecResult` is a **namedtuple** `(exit_code, output)`: production unpacks it in `_fold_session_usage` (`exit_code, output = …exec_run(…)` → "cannot unpack non-iterable types.SimpleNamespace") while reading attributes elsewhere. Both fakes also lack `get_archive` (the issue #1339 session export calls `session.container.get_archive` → "'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'get_archive'"). Not a production regression: the production call shapes match the real docker API; the fakes predate the #1339 export and the fold's unpack. ~18 warning pairs across otherwise-passing tests.

3. **Stale REG in the third bench root (AC4 blocker)** — `bench/mls_bench/test_build_run.py::RegressionPinsTest::test_bench_harbor_family_anchors` pins the pre-#1316 default dataset literal `terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0`; #1316 deliberately moved the bench-harbor default to `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest`. Same rot class as the ticket's systemic lesson: mls_bench is only executed by bench-mls.yml's dispatch-gated setup, so the drift sat invisible.

**Impact**: every bench-harbor/bench dispatch dies at setup (`errors=1`) — shards never start; the warnings bury real signal in trial logs; any PR touching bench/ ships untested python.

**Fix approach**:
1. Skip only the usage fold for never-started modes; keep the gh-1576 audit write (the raw failure-mode string IS the truthful outcome). Parity with the harbor adapter holds (harbor always writes the audit on every termination path).
2. Make both fakes faithful to docker-py: namedtuple `ExecResult` (unpack + attribute access both work) and a `get_archive` returning `([valid_tar], stat)`.
3. Update the stale REG to pin the shipped #1316 default (2.1), keeping the agent/MLS-free anchors.
4. Systemic guard: new path-filtered workflow `.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml` running the exact setup gate (same pinned deps: `harbor[modal]==0.23.0`, `terminal-bench==0.2.18`, python 3.13) on every PR and main push touching `bench/**`.

{"content":"# gh-1638 AC4 (the systemic lesson): the bench-script python tests ran
# ONLY inside the bench workflows' setup jobs (dispatch-gated), so the
# Oct-14 merge wave rotted them on main invisibly for 3+ days — every
# dispatch died at setup while the main quality gate (dart test / coverage
# / guards) never executes a line of python. This job runs the EXACT setup
# gate (same discovery roots, same pinned deps) on every bench/** change:
# a red bench-script test now fails the PR and main cannot rot silently.
name: Bench script tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Superseded PR runs die instantly; main-push runs are never cancelled
# mid-flight (same release-protection principle as ci.yml).
concurrency:
  group: Bench script tests-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal permissions.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  unit-tests:
    name: Unit-test bench scripts
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # terminal-bench-era note (bench-harbor.yml): harbor is fine on 3.13;
      # typer-based CLIs break on 3.14.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned exactly like the bench workflows' setup gate: the adapters
      # target the harbor 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent / terminal-bench 0.2.18
      # import surfaces.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0' 'terminal-bench==0.2.18'

      # Same gate as bench.yml / bench-harbor.yml "Unit-test bench scripts"
      # (plus the bench-mls.yml root — all three bench discovery roots);
      # keep the step bodies in sync with those workflows.
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
        run: |
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/mls_bench -v
","path":".github/workflows/bench-tests.yml"}

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1638

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `test_other_failure_modes_stay_raw_in_the_stock_audit` fails on main with `FileNotFoundError: …/fa-agent-timeout.json` (bench-harbor setup job red since the Oct-14 wave), plus dozens of `session usage extraction failed` / `fa session export failed` warnings polluting the same log, plus a stale REG red in `bench/mls_bench`.

**Root cause** (three independent rots, all in `bench/`):

1. **Audit writer gap (AC1)** — `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py`, `FaAgent.perform_task`, stock/unsupervised path. The gh-1209 never-started guard
   ```python
   if result.failure_mode in _NEVER_STARTED_MODES:
       return result
   ```
   early-returns BEFORE the gh-1576 (I2) audit write. `_NEVER_STARTED_MODES = {AGENT_INSTALLATION_FAILED, UNKNOWN_AGENT_ERROR}`, so with a known external cap the audit file is never written for exactly the "other failure modes" the gh-1576 contract says must land **raw** — the `else str(result.failure_mode.value)` branch of the same audit call is dead code for those modes. The writer's own comment ("with an external cap known, even this unsupervised termination lands the audit") states the contract the early return violates. Reproduced locally with CI parity: `python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench` → `Ran 410 tests … FAILED (errors=1)`, same FileNotFoundError.

2. **Unfaithful docker fakes (AC2)** — `FakeTmuxSession.container` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`) and `FakeContainer` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_progress_watch_adapter.py`) return `types.SimpleNamespace(exit_code=…, output=…)` from `exec_run`, but docker-py's `ExecResult` is a **namedtuple** `(exit_code, output)`: production unpacks it in `_fold_session_usage` (`exit_code, output = …exec_run(…)` → "cannot unpack non-iterable types.SimpleNamespace") while reading attributes elsewhere. Both fakes also lack `get_archive` (the issue #1339 session export calls `session.container.get_archive` → "'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'get_archive'"). Not a production regression: the production call shapes match the real docker API; the fakes predate the #1339 export and the fold's unpack. ~18 warning pairs across otherwise-passing tests.

3. **Stale REG in the third bench root (AC4 blocker)** — `bench/mls_bench/test_build_run.py::RegressionPinsTest::test_bench_harbor_family_anchors` pins the pre-#1316 default dataset literal `terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0`; #1316 deliberately moved the bench-harbor default to `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest`. Same rot class as the ticket's systemic lesson: mls_bench is only executed by bench-mls.yml's dispatch-gated setup, so the drift sat invisible.

**Impact**: every bench-harbor/bench dispatch dies at setup (`errors=1`) — shards never start; the warnings bury real signal in trial logs; any PR touching bench/ ships untested python.

**Fix approach**:
1. Skip only the usage fold for never-started modes; keep the gh-1576 audit write (the raw failure-mode string IS the truthful outcome). Parity with the harbor adapter holds (harbor always writes the audit on every termination path).
2. Make both fakes faithful to docker-py: namedtuple `ExecResult` (unpack + attribute access both work) and a `get_archive` returning `([valid_tar], stat)`.
3. Update the stale REG to pin the shipped #1316 default (2.1), keeping the agent/MLS-free anchors.
4. Systemic guard: new path-filtered workflow `.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml` running the exact setup gate (same pinned deps: `harbor[modal]==0.23.0`, `terminal-bench==0.2.18`, python 3.13) on every PR and main push touching `bench/**`.

{"content":"# gh-1638 AC4 (the systemic lesson): the bench-script python tests ran
# ONLY inside the bench workflows' setup jobs (dispatch-gated), so the
# Oct-14 merge wave rotted them on main invisibly for 3+ days — every
# dispatch died at setup while the main quality gate (dart test / coverage
# / guards) never executes a line of python. This job runs the EXACT setup
# gate (same discovery roots, same pinned deps) on every bench/** change:
# a red bench-script test now fails the PR and main cannot rot silently.
name: Bench script tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Superseded PR runs die instantly; main-push runs are never cancelled
# mid-flight (same release-protection principle as ci.yml).
concurrency:
  group: Bench script tests-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal permissions.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  unit-tests:
    name: Unit-test bench scripts
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # terminal-bench-era note (bench-harbor.yml): harbor is fine on 3.13;
      # typer-based CLIs break on 3.14.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned exactly like the bench workflows' setup gate: the adapters
      # target the harbor 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent / terminal-bench 0.2.18
      # import surfaces.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0' 'terminal-bench==0.2.18'

      # Same gate as bench.yml / bench-harbor.yml "Unit-test bench scripts"
      # (plus the bench-mls.yml root — all three bench discovery roots);
      # keep the step bodies in sync with those workflows.
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
        run: |
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/mls_bench -v
","path":".github/workflows/bench-tests.yml"}

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `test_other_failure_modes_stay_raw_in_the_stock_audit` fails on main with `FileNotFoundError: …/fa-agent-timeout.json` (bench-harbor setup job red since the Oct-14 wave), plus dozens of `session usage extraction failed` / `fa session export failed` warnings polluting the same log, plus a stale REG red in `bench/mls_bench`.

**Root cause** (three independent rots, all in `bench/`):

1. **Audit writer gap (AC1)** — `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py`, `FaAgent.perform_task`, stock/unsupervised path. The gh-1209 never-started guard
   ```python
   if result.failure_mode in _NEVER_STARTED_MODES:
       return result
   ```
   early-returns BEFORE the gh-1576 (I2) audit write. `_NEVER_STARTED_MODES = {AGENT_INSTALLATION_FAILED, UNKNOWN_AGENT_ERROR}`, so with a known external cap the audit file is never written for exactly the "other failure modes" the gh-1576 contract says must land **raw** — the `else str(result.failure_mode.value)` branch of the same audit call is dead code for those modes. The writer's own comment ("with an external cap known, even this unsupervised termination lands the audit") states the contract the early return violates. Reproduced locally with CI parity: `python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench` → `Ran 410 tests … FAILED (errors=1)`, same FileNotFoundError.

2. **Unfaithful docker fakes (AC2)** — `FakeTmuxSession.container` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`) and `FakeContainer` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_progress_watch_adapter.py`) return `types.SimpleNamespace(exit_code=…, output=…)` from `exec_run`, but docker-py's `ExecResult` is a **namedtuple** `(exit_code, output)`: production unpacks it in `_fold_session_usage` (`exit_code, output = …exec_run(…)` → "cannot unpack non-iterable types.SimpleNamespace") while reading attributes elsewhere. Both fakes also lack `get_archive` (the issue #1339 session export calls `session.container.get_archive` → "'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'get_archive'"). Not a production regression: the production call shapes match the real docker API; the fakes predate the #1339 export and the fold's unpack. ~18 warning pairs across otherwise-passing tests.

3. **Stale REG in the third bench root (AC4 blocker)** — `bench/mls_bench/test_build_run.py::RegressionPinsTest::test_bench_harbor_family_anchors` pins the pre-#1316 default dataset literal `terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0`; #1316 deliberately moved the bench-harbor default to `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest`. Same rot class as the ticket's systemic lesson: mls_bench is only executed by bench-mls.yml's dispatch-gated setup, so the drift sat invisible.

**Impact**: every bench-harbor/bench dispatch dies at setup (`errors=1`) — shards never start; the warnings bury real signal in trial logs; any PR touching bench/ ships untested python.

**Fix approach**:
1. Skip only the usage fold for never-started modes; keep the gh-1576 audit write (the raw failure-mode string IS the truthful outcome). Parity with the harbor adapter holds (harbor always writes the audit on every termination path).

4. Systemic guard: new path-filtered workflow `.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml` running the exact setup gate (same pinned deps: `harbor[modal]==0.23.0`, `terminal-bench==0.2.18`, python 3.13) on every PR and main push touching `bench/**`.

{"content":"# gh-1638 AC4 (the systemic lesson): the bench-script python tests ran
# ONLY inside the bench workflows' setup jobs (dispatch-gated), so the
# Oct-14 merge wave rotted them on main invisibly for 3+ days — every
# dispatch died at setup while the main quality gate (dart test / coverage
# / guards) never executes a line of python. This job runs the EXACT setup
# gate (same discovery roots, same pinned deps) on every bench/** change:
# a red bench-script test now fails the PR and main cannot rot silently.
name: Bench script tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Superseded PR runs die instantly; main-push runs are never cancelled
# mid-flight (same release-protection principle as ci.yml).
concurrency:
  group: Bench script tests-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal permissions.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  unit-tests:
    name: Unit-test bench scripts
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # terminal-bench-era note (bench-harbor.yml): harbor is fine on 3.13;
      # typer-based CLIs break on 3.14.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned exactly like the bench workflows' setup gate: the adapters
      # target the harbor 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent / terminal-bench 0.2.18
      # import surfaces.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0' 'terminal-bench==0.2.18'

      # Same gate as bench.yml / bench-harbor.yml "Unit-test bench scripts"
      # (plus the bench-mls.yml root — all three bench discovery roots);
      # keep the step bodies in sync with those workflows.
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts

def _real_harbor_available() -> bool:
    """True when the REAL harbor package is importable.

    gh-1535: the stub below must NOT clobber a real harbor install.
    `unittest discover` imports every test module in this directory
    before running any test, so an unconditional _stub_harbor() parks a
    synthetic BaseInstalledAgent (a bare type with no __init__) in
    sys.modules; HarborParityTest / HarnessArtifactIsolationTest in
    test_fa_agent_timeout then load bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py against
    that stub and `FaAgent(logs_dir)` dies with "takes no arguments".
    The stub modules built by _module() are bare types.ModuleType objects
    with no __file__; the real harbor package always has one.
    """
    try:
        module = importlib.import_module("harbor.agents.installed.base")
    except ImportError as e:
        # gh-1535 rework: a missing TRANSITIVE dep (e.g. pydantic with a
        # --no-deps harbor install) means harbor is present but broken —
        # fail loudly rather than silently stubbing over it and
        # recreating the original "FaAgent() takes no arguments" CI shape.
        if e.name is not None and not e.name.startswith("harbor"):
            raise
        return False
    return getattr(module, "__file__", None) is not None


def _harbor_distribution_present() -> bool:
    """True when a `harbor` distribution is installed, importable or not.

    Distinguishes "harbor not installed" (tests may skip) from "harbor
    installed but the sys.modules stub is bound" — the gh-1535 regression,
    which must FAIL loudly. Distribution metadata is the signal (not
    find_spec: a parked stub module has __spec__ None, so find_spec raises
    ValueError and cannot answer the question).
    """
    try:
        return importlib.metadata.distribution("harbor") is not None
    except importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError:

def _load(name, path):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules[name] = module
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    # gh-1537: NO `branches: [main]` here — the post-merge main CI run is
    # retired. The SM's pre-merge validation dispatch (machine-sm.yml ->
    # factory-sm, strictly serialized) validates the exact tree that
    # merges, so a main-push run would be pure repetition; retiring it
    # kills the duplicate wall time AND the release-bot-commit churn that
    # retriggered it (#1522 lands the tag-sourced versions). The v* tag
    # push stays: the release pipeline (publish/binaries) keys on it, and
    # the full quality gate runs on the tag BEFORE anything publishes.
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `test_other_failure_modes_stay_raw_in_the_stock_audit` fails on main with `FileNotFoundError: …/fa-agent-timeout.json` (bench-harbor setup job red since the Oct-14 wave), plus dozens of `session usage extraction failed` / `fa session export failed` warnings polluting the same log, plus a stale REG red in `bench/mls_bench`.

**Root cause** (three independent rots, all in `bench/`):

1. **Audit writer gap (AC1)** — `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py`, `FaAgent.perform_task`, stock/unsupervised path. The gh-1209 never-started guard
   ```python
   if result.failure_mode in _NEVER_STARTED_MODES:
       return result
   ```
   early-returns BEFORE the gh-1576 (I2) audit write. `_NEVER_STARTED_MODES = {AGENT_INSTALLATION_FAILED, UNKNOWN_AGENT_ERROR}`, so with a known external cap the audit file is never written for exactly the "other failure modes" the gh-1576 contract says must land **raw** — the `else str(result.failure_mode.value)` branch of the same audit call is dead code for those modes. The writer's own comment ("with an external cap known, even this unsupervised termination lands the audit") states the contract the early return violates. Reproduced locally with CI parity: `python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench` → `Ran 410 tests … FAILED (errors=1)`, same FileNotFoundError.

2. **Unfaithful docker fakes (AC2)** — `FakeTmuxSession.container` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`) and `FakeContainer` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_progress_watch_adapter.py`) return `types.SimpleNamespace(exit_code=…, output=…)` from `exec_run`, but docker-py's `ExecResult` is a **namedtuple** `(exit_code, output)`: production unpacks it in `_fold_session_usage` (`exit_code, output = …exec_run(…)` → "cannot unpack non-iterable types.SimpleNamespace") while reading attributes elsewhere. Both fakes also lack `get_archive` (the issue #1339 session export calls `session.container.get_archive` → "'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'get_archive'"). Not a production regression: the production call shapes match the real docker API; the fakes predate the #1339 export and the fold's unpack. ~18 warning pairs across otherwise-passing tests.

3. **Stale REG in the third bench root (AC4 blocker)** — `bench/mls_bench/test_build_run.py::RegressionPinsTest::test_bench_harbor_family_anchors` pins the pre-#1316 default dataset literal `terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0`; #1316 deliberately moved the bench-harbor default to `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest`. Same rot class as the ticket's systemic lesson: mls_bench is only executed by bench-mls.yml's dispatch-gated setup, so the drift sat invisible.

**Impact**: every bench-harbor/bench dispatch dies at setup (`errors=1`) — shards never start; the warnings bury real signal in trial logs; any PR touching bench/ ships untested python.

**Fix approach**:
1. Skip only the usage fold for never-started modes; keep the gh-1576 audit write (the raw failure-mode string IS the truthful outcome). Parity with the harbor adapter holds (harbor always writes the audit on every termination path).
2. Make both fakes faithful to docker-py: namedtuple `ExecResult` (unpack + attribute access both work) and a `get_archive` returning `([valid_tar], stat)`.
3. Update the stale REG to pin the shipped #1316 default (2.1), keeping the agent/MLS-free anchors.
4. Systemic guard: new path-filtered workflow `.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml` running the exact setup gate (same pinned deps: `harbor[modal]==0.23.0`, `terminal-bench==0.2.18`, python 3.13) on every PR and main push touching `bench/**`.

{"content":"# gh-1638 AC4 (the systemic lesson): the bench-script python tests ran
# ONLY inside the bench workflows' setup jobs (dispatch-gated), so the

name: Bench script tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'

# mid-flight (same release-protection principle as ci.yml).
concurrency:

  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

          python -m unittest discover -s bench/mls_bench -v

def _real_harbor_available() -> bool:
    """True when the REAL harbor package is importable.

    gh-1535: the stub below must NOT clobber a real harbor install.
    `unittest discover` imports every test module in this directory
    before running any test, so an unconditional _stub_harbor() parks a
    synthetic BaseInstalledAgent (a bare type with no __init__) in
    sys.modules; HarborParityTest / HarnessArtifactIsolationTest in
    test_fa_agent_timeout then load bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py against
    that stub and `FaAgent(logs_dir)` dies with "takes no arguments".
    The stub modules built by _module() are bare types.ModuleType objects
    with no __file__; the real harbor package always has one.
    """
    try:
        module = importlib.import_module("harbor.agents.installed.base")
    except ImportError as e:
        # gh-1535 rework: a missing TRANSITIVE dep (e.g. pydantic with a
        # --no-deps harbor install) means harbor is present but broken —
        # fail loudly rather than silently stubbing over it and
        # recreating the original "FaAgent() takes no arguments" CI shape.
        if e.name is not None and not e.name.startswith("harbor"):

    return getattr(module, "__file__", None) is not None

# Headless-Chrome acceptance suite for the browser extension (issue #23):
# builds the extension zip, runs the Node vm-sandbox unit tests, then the

name: Browser extension

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'browser_ext/e2e/**'
      - 'lib/src/browser/**'
      - 'bin/serve_bridge.dart'
      - 'test/browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'

  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'browser_ext/e2e/**'

      - 'test/browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'

# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.
# Results upload

# wiring), kimi-for-coding (model id == plan name; FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY), or

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:

        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1503, same contract as bench.yml gh-1471: default = pre-gh-1503 behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1638

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `test_other_failure_modes_stay_raw_in_the_stock_audit` fails on main with `FileNotFoundError: …/fa-agent-timeout.json` (bench-harbor setup job red since the Oct-14 wave), plus dozens of `session usage extraction failed` / `fa session export failed` warnings polluting the same log, plus a stale REG red in `bench/mls_bench`.

**Root cause** (three independent rots, all in `bench/`):

1. **Audit writer gap (AC1)** — `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py`, `FaAgent.perform_task`, stock/unsupervised path. The gh-1209 never-started guard
   ```python
   if result.failure_mode in _NEVER_STARTED_MODES:
       return result
   ```
   early-returns BEFORE the gh-1576 (I2) audit write. `_NEVER_STARTED_MODES = {AGENT_INSTALLATION_FAILED, UNKNOWN_AGENT_ERROR}`, so with a known external cap the audit file is never written for exactly the "other failure modes" the gh-1576 contract says must land **raw** — the `else str(result.failure_mode.value)` branch of the same audit call is dead code for those modes. The writer's own comment ("with an external cap known, even this unsupervised termination lands the audit") states the contract the early return violates. Reproduced locally with CI parity: `python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench` → `Ran 410 tests … FAILED (errors=1)`, same FileNotFoundError.

2. **Unfaithful docker fakes (AC2)** — `FakeTmuxSession.container` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`) and `FakeContainer` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_progress_watch_adapter.py`) return `types.SimpleNamespace(exit_code=…, output=…)` from `exec_run`, but docker-py's `ExecResult` is a **namedtuple** `(exit_code, output)`: production unpacks it in `_fold_session_usage` (`exit_code, output = …exec_run(…)` → "cannot unpack non-iterable types.SimpleNamespace") while reading attributes elsewhere. Both fakes also lack `get_archive` (the issue #1339 session export calls `session.container.get_archive` → "'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'get_archive'"). Not a production regression: the production call shapes match the real docker API; the fakes predate the #1339 export and the fold's unpack. ~18 warning pairs across otherwise-passing tests.

3. **Stale REG in the third bench root (AC4 blocker)** — `bench/mls_bench/test_build_run.py::RegressionPinsTest::test_bench_harbor_family_anchors` pins the pre-#1316 default dataset literal `terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0`; #1316 deliberately moved the bench-harbor default to `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest`. Same rot class as the ticket's systemic lesson: mls_bench is only executed by bench-mls.yml's dispatch-gated setup, so the drift sat invisible.

**Impact**: every bench-harbor/bench dispatch dies at setup (`errors=1`) — shards never start; the warnings bury real signal in trial logs; any PR touching bench/ ships untested python.

**Fix approach**:
1. Skip only the usage fold for never-started modes; keep the gh-1576 audit write (the raw failure-mode string IS the truthful outcome). Parity with the harbor adapter holds (harbor always writes the audit on every termination path).
2. Make both fakes faithful to docker-py: namedtuple `ExecResult` (unpack + attribute access both work) and a `get_archive` returning `([valid_tar], stat)`.
3. Update the stale REG to pin the shipped #1316 default (2.1), keeping the agent/MLS-free anchors.
4. Systemic guard: new path-filtered workflow `.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml` running the exact setup gate (same pinned deps: `harbor[modal]==0.23.0`, `terminal-bench==0.2.18`, python 3.13) on every PR and main push touching `bench/**`.

**Previous attempt**: none (first fix for gh-1638).

{"content":"# gh-1638 AC4 (the systemic lesson): the bench-script python tests ran
# ONLY inside the bench workflows' setup jobs (dispatch-gated), so the
# Oct-14 merge wave rotted them on main invisibly for 3+ days — every
# dispatch died at setup while the main quality gate (dart test / coverage
# / guards) never executes a line of python. This job runs the EXACT setup
# gate (same discovery roots, same pinned deps) on every bench/** change:
# a red bench-script test now fails the PR and main cannot rot silently.
name: Bench script tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Superseded PR runs die instantly; main-push runs are never cancelled
# mid-flight (same release-protection principle as ci.yml).
concurrency:
  group: Bench script tests-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal permissions.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  unit-tests:
    name: Unit-test bench scripts
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # terminal-bench-era note (bench-harbor.yml): harbor is fine on 3.13;
      # typer-based CLIs break on 3.14.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned exactly like the bench workflows' setup gate: the adapters
      # target the harbor 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent / terminal-bench 0.2.18
      # import surfaces.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0' 'terminal-bench==0.2.18'

      # Same gate as bench.yml / bench-harbor.yml "Unit-test bench scripts"
      # (plus the bench-mls.yml root — all three bench discovery roots);
      # keep the step bodies in sync with those workflows.
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
        run: |
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/mls_bench -v

class FaAgentTest(unittest.TestCase):
    class AgentResult:
        def __init__(self, total_input_tokens=0, total_output_tokens=0, failure_mode="none"):
            self.total_input_tokens = total_input_tokens
            self.total_output_tokens = total_output_tokens
            self.failure_mode = failure_mode

    class FakeSession:
        class Container:
            def __init__(self, text):
                self.text = text

            def exec_run(self, cmd):
                return 0, self.text.encode()

        def __init__(self, text):
            self.copy_calls = 0
            self.container = self.Container(text)

        def copy_to_container(self, *args, **kwargs):
            self.copy_calls += 1

    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.sessions = make_sessions(Path(self.tmp.name))
        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)

    def legacy_agent(self):
        agent = legacy_fa_agent.FaAgent.__new__(legacy_fa_agent.FaAgent)
        agent._bundle_tarball = Path("unused.tar.gz")  # __new__ skips __init__
        return agent

    def legacy_result(self, text):
        agent = self.legacy_agent()
        return agent.perform_task("do it", self.FakeSession(text)), agent

    def test_ut1_legacy_adapter_sums_known_usage(self):
        result, _ = self.legacy_result(MAIN_SESSION + SUBAGENT_SESSION)
        self.assertEqual(result.total_input_tokens, EXPECTED_IN)
        self.assertEqual(result.total_output_tokens, EXPECTED_OUT)

    def test_ut1_legacy_adapter_reads_container_via_find(self):
        session = self.FakeSession(MAIN_SESSION)
        agent = self.legacy_agent()
        agent.perform_task("do it", session)
        self.assertEqual(session.copy_calls, 1)

    def test_ut1_harbor_adapter_sums_known_usage_and_cost(self):
        agent = harbor_fa_agent.FaAgent.__new__(harbor_fa_agent.FaAgent)
        agent.logs_dir = self.sessions.parent
        context = harbor_fa_agent.AgentContext()
        agent.populate_context_post_run(context)
        # Harbor semantics: n_input_tokens includes cache.
        self.assertEqual(context.n_input_tokens, EXPECTED_IN + EXPECTED_CR + EXPECTED_CW)
        self.assertEqual(context.n_output_tokens, EXPECTED_OUT)
        self.assertEqual(context.n_cache_tokens, EXPECTED_CR + EXPECTED_CW)
        self.assertEqual(result.total_output_tokens, 0)

    def test_installation_failure_result_untouched(self):
        original = self.AgentResult(failure_mode="agent_installation_failed")
        agent = self.legacy_agent()
        monkey = unittest.mock.patch.object(
            legacy_fa_agent.AbstractInstalledAgent,
            "perform_task",
            return_value=original,
        )
        with monkey:
            result = agent.perform_task("do it", no_exec_session("agent_installation_failed"))
        self.assertIs(result, original)

    def test_timeout_result_folds_session_usage(self):
        # gh-1209: a timed-out run is the EXPENSIVE run — the session usage
        # fold must run for any outcome where fa actually ran, not only for
        # healthy results. tb's harness discards the adapter's result on its
        # own timeout and records its own zeros, so whenever a timeout
        # result does round-trip through perform_task, it must carry the
        # session's real numbers.
        original = self.AgentResult(failure_mode="agent_timeout")
        agent = self.legacy_agent()
        session = self.FakeSession(MAIN_SESSION + SUBAGENT_SESSION)
        monkey = unittest.mock.patch.object(
            legacy_fa_agent.AbstractInstalledAgent,
            "perform_task",
            return_value=original,
        )
        with monkey:
            result = agent.perform_task("do it", session)
        self.assertEqual(result.total_input_tokens, EXPECTED_IN)
        self.assertEqual(result.total_output_tokens, EXPECTED_OUT)

    def test_unknown_agent_error_result_untouched(self):
        # gh-1209: unknown_agent_error is a true never-started trial — the
        # harness never got the agent going, so there is nothing to fold
        # and the result passes through byte-for-byte.
        original = self.AgentResult(failure_mode="unknown_agent_error")
        agent = self.legacy_agent()
        monkey = unittest.mock.patch.object(
            legacy_fa_agent.AbstractInstalledAgent,
            "perform_task",
            return_value=original,
        )
        with monkey:
            result = agent.perform_task("do it", no_exec_session("unknown_agent_error"))
        self.assertIs(result, original)

    def test_other_ran_failure_mode_folds_session_usage(self):
        # gh-1209 review: pins the DEFAULT-FOLD direction. agent_timeout
        # alone cannot distinguish "fold for any ran outcome" from a future
        # accidental fold-whitelist (mode in _FOLD_MODES); a ran-outcome
        # mode outside the stub's named set must fold too.
        original = self.AgentResult(failure_mode="parse_error")
        agent = self.legacy_agent()
        session = self.FakeSession(MAIN_SESSION + SUBAGENT_SESSION)
        monkey = unittest.mock.patch.object(
            legacy_fa_agent.AbstractInstalledAgent,
            "perform_task",
            return_value=original,
        )
        with monkey:
            result = agent.perform_task("do it", session)
        self.assertEqual(result.total_input_tokens, EXPECTED_IN)
        self.assertEqual(result.total_output_tokens, EXPECTED_OUT)

class HarborStubHygieneTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """gh-1535 regression: the harbor sys.modules stub in this module must
    not poison tests loaded later in the same `unittest discover` process.

    HarborParityTest / HarnessArtifactIsolationTest (test_fa_agent_timeout)
    exec bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py and construct FaAgent(logs_dir); when

    (logs_dir, ...) constructor — the bare-stub base raises
    "FaAgent() takes no arguments". When harbor is absent this module's
    own ITs still run against the stub, so nothing is skipped there.
    """

    def test_fa_agent_binds_real_base_when_harbor_installed(self):
        if not _real_harbor_available():
            # gh-1535 rework: never silently disengage in the regressed
            # state. An installed harbor distribution whose import resolves
            # to the stub parked in sys.modules IS the bug — fail with the

            if _harbor_distribution_present():

                    "harbor is installed but the sys.modules stub is bound"
                    " (gh-1535 regression: FaAgent(logs_dir) would raise"
                    " 'takes no arguments' in test_fa_agent_timeout)"
                )
            self.skipTest("real harbor not installed")
        import harbor.agents.installed.base as real_base

        self.assertIs(
            harbor_fa_agent.BaseInstalledAgent, real_base.BaseInstalledAgent
        )
        # gh-1535: exercise the REAL constructor shape the parity suite
        # uses — FaAgent(logs_dir). __new__ + attribute assignment would
        # pass even against the bare-stub base (no __init__), masking the
        # regression this test exists to catch.
        agent = harbor_fa_agent.FaAgent(Path("/nonexistent/logs"))
        self.assertEqual(agent.logs_dir, Path("/nonexistent/logs"))

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1638

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `test_other_failure_modes_stay_raw_in_the_stock_audit` fails on main with `FileNotFoundError: …/fa-agent-timeout.json` (bench-harbor setup job red since the Oct-14 wave), plus dozens of `session usage extraction failed` / `fa session export failed` warnings polluting the same log, plus a stale REG red in `bench/mls_bench`.

**Root cause** (three independent rots, all in `bench/`):

1. **Audit writer gap (AC1)** — `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py`, `FaAgent.perform_task`, stock/unsupervised path. The gh-1209 never-started guard
   ```python
   if result.failure_mode in _NEVER_STARTED_MODES:
       return result
   ```
   early-returns BEFORE the gh-1576 (I2) audit write. `_NEVER_STARTED_MODES = {AGENT_INSTALLATION_FAILED, UNKNOWN_AGENT_ERROR}`, so with a known external cap the audit file is never written for exactly the "other failure modes" the gh-1576 contract says must land **raw** — the `else str(result.failure_mode.value)` branch of the same audit call is dead code for those modes. The writer's own comment ("with an external cap known, even this unsupervised termination lands the audit") states the contract the early return violates. Reproduced locally with CI parity: `python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench` → `Ran 410 tests … FAILED (errors=1)`, same FileNotFoundError.

2. **Unfaithful docker fakes (AC2)** — `FakeTmuxSession.container` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py`) and `FakeContainer` (`bench/terminal_bench/test_progress_watch_adapter.py`) return `types.SimpleNamespace(exit_code=…, output=…)` from `exec_run`, but docker-py's `ExecResult` is a **namedtuple** `(exit_code, output)`: production unpacks it in `_fold_session_usage` (`exit_code, output = …exec_run(…)` → "cannot unpack non-iterable types.SimpleNamespace") while reading attributes elsewhere. Both fakes also lack `get_archive` (the issue #1339 session export calls `session.container.get_archive` → "'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'get_archive'"). Not a production regression: the production call shapes match the real docker API; the fakes predate the #1339 export and the fold's unpack. ~18 warning pairs across otherwise-passing tests.

3. **Stale REG in the third bench root (AC4 blocker)** — `bench/mls_bench/test_build_run.py::RegressionPinsTest::test_bench_harbor_family_anchors` pins the pre-#1316 default dataset literal `terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0`; #1316 deliberately moved the bench-harbor default to `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest`. Same rot class as the ticket's systemic lesson: mls_bench is only executed by bench-mls.yml's dispatch-gated setup, so the drift sat invisible.

**Impact**: every bench-harbor/bench dispatch dies at setup (`errors=1`) — shards never start; the warnings bury real signal in trial logs; any PR touching bench/ ships untested python.

**Fix approach**:
1. Skip only the usage fold for never-started modes; keep the gh-1576 audit write (the raw failure-mode string IS the truthful outcome). Parity with the harbor adapter holds (harbor always writes the audit on every termination path).
2. Make both fakes faithful to docker-py: namedtuple `ExecResult` (unpack + attribute access both work) and a `get_archive` returning `([valid_tar], stat)`.
3. Update the stale REG to pin the shipped #1316 default (2.1), keeping the agent/MLS-free anchors.
4. Systemic guard: new path-filtered workflow `.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml` running the exact setup gate (same pinned deps: `harbor[modal]==0.23.0`, `terminal-bench==0.2.18`, python 3.13) on every PR and main push touching `bench/**`.

{"content":"# gh-1638 AC4 (the systemic lesson): the bench-script python tests ran
# ONLY inside the bench workflows' setup jobs (dispatch-gated), so the
# Oct-14 merge wave rotted them on main invisibly for 3+ days — every
# dispatch died at setup while the main quality gate (dart test / coverage
# / guards) never executes a line of python. This job runs the EXACT setup
# gate (same discovery roots, same pinned deps) on every bench/** change:
# a red bench-script test now fails the PR and main cannot rot silently.
name: Bench script tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'bench/**'
      - '.github/workflows/bench-tests.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Superseded PR runs die instantly; main-push runs are never cancelled
# mid-flight (same release-protection principle as ci.yml).
concurrency:
  group: Bench script tests-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal permissions.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  unit-tests:
    name: Unit-test bench scripts
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # terminal-bench-era note (bench-harbor.yml): harbor is fine on 3.13;
      # typer-based CLIs break on 3.14.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned exactly like the bench workflows' setup gate: the adapters
      # target the harbor 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent / terminal-bench 0.2.18
      # import surfaces.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0' 'terminal-bench==0.2.18'

      # Same gate as bench.yml / bench-harbor.yml "Unit-test bench scripts"
      # (plus the bench-mls.yml root — all three bench discovery roots);
      # keep the step bodies in sync with those workflows.
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
        run: |
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/mls_bench -v
","path":".github/workflows/bench-tests.yml"}

def _real_harbor_available() -> bool:
    """True when the REAL harbor package is importable.

    gh-1535: the stub below must NOT clobber a real harbor install.
    `unittest discover` imports every test module in this directory
    before running any test, so an unconditional _stub_harbor() parks a
    synthetic BaseInstalledAgent (a bare type with no __init__) in
    sys.modules; HarborParityTest / HarnessArtifactIsolationTest in
    test_fa_agent_timeout then load bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py against
    that stub and `FaAgent(logs_dir)` dies with "takes no arguments".
    The stub modules built by _module() are bare types.ModuleType objects
    with no __file__; the real harbor package always has one.
    """
    try:
        module = importlib.import_module("harbor.agents.installed.base")
    except ImportError as e:
        # gh-1535 rework: a missing TRANSITIVE dep (e.g. pydantic with a
        # --no-deps harbor install) means harbor is present but broken —
        # fail loudly rather than silently stubbing over it and
        # recreating the original "FaAgent() takes no arguments" CI shape.
        if e.name is not None and not e.name.startswith("harbor"):
            raise
        return False
    return getattr(module, "__file__", None) is not None


def _harbor_distribution_present() -> bool:
    """True when a `harbor` distribution is installed, importable or not.

    Distinguishes "harbor not installed" (tests may skip) from "harbor
    installed but the sys.modules stub is bound" — the gh-1535 regression,
    which must FAIL loudly. Distribution metadata is the signal (not
    find_spec: a parked stub module has __spec__ None, so find_spec raises
    ValueError and cannot answer the question).
    """
    try:
        return importlib.metadata.distribution("harbor") is not None
    except importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
        return False

def _load(name, path):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules[name] = module
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module
